The Operating Agreement provides that additional capital contributions may be called by the Managing Member upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to all Members. Members who fail to fund additional capital calls within the required period are subject to dilution of their Membership Interest in accordance with a dilution formula set forth in the Operating Agreement. \[Redacted: Detailed dilution mechanics omitted from this summary.\]

The Operating Agreement does not appear to require unanimous consent or approval of a supermajority of Members for the issuance of capital calls. Rather, the Managing Member has unilateral authority to determine the timing, amount, and purpose of additional capital calls, subject only to the overall purpose clause of the Company and any limitations imposed by the annual budget approval process described in Section 3.2.

**2.3 Capital Accounts**

\[Redacted --- Capital account maintenance provisions omitted from this summary. Borrower\'s counsel notes that capital accounts are maintained in accordance with Treasury Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv).\]

**[Section 3: Management]{.underline}**

**3.1 Managing Member**

Graydon Development Group LLC (\"**GDG**\") serves as the Managing Member of the Company. The Operating Agreement provides that GDG has \"exclusive and sole authority to manage the day-to-day business and affairs of the Company,\" subject only to those matters requiring the approval of the Members as set forth in Section 3.2 (Major Decisions). Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Operating Agreement vests the Managing Member with the authority to perform the following functions on behalf of the Company:

> \(a\) Negotiating and executing leases of space within the Property on behalf of the Company;
>
> \(b\) Engaging and overseeing contractors, consultants, architects, engineers, and property managers in connection with the renovation, improvement, and operation of the Property;
>
> \(c\) Making capital calls on the Members in accordance with Section 2.2;
>
> \(d\) Opening and maintaining bank accounts in the name of the Company at such financial institutions as the Managing Member shall determine;
>
> \(e\) Executing loan documents, promissory notes, deeds of trust, mortgages, security agreements, guaranties, and related instruments on behalf of the Company;
>
> \(f\) Making distributions to the Members in accordance with Section 5 of the Operating Agreement;
>
> \(g\) Preparing and filing (or causing to be prepared and filed) federal, state, and local tax returns and making tax elections on behalf of the Company;
>
> \(h\) Engaging legal counsel, accountants, appraisers, and other professionals on behalf of the Company as the Managing Member deems necessary or appropriate.

Neil Ashford Graydon, as the sole member and sole manager of GDG, has the authority to act on behalf of GDG in its capacity as Managing Member of the Company. The Operating Agreement does not impose any requirement for GDG to appoint or maintain an independent director, independent manager, or springing member. There is no provision within the Operating Agreement requiring the consent of any independent party prior to the Company filing a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any state insolvency proceeding. The Operating Agreement does not contain any bankruptcy remoteness provisions or any requirement that the Company maintain its existence as a single-purpose entity separate and apart from its Members.

**3.2 Major Decisions Requiring Member Approval**

Notwithstanding the Managing Member\'s broad authority as described in Section 3.1, the Operating Agreement provides that the following \"**Major Decisions**\" require the prior written approval of Members holding at least **seventy-five percent (75%)** of the outstanding Membership Interests:

> \(i\) The sale, exchange, or other disposition of all or substantially all of the Property;
>
> \(ii\) Any financing or refinancing of the Property in an amount in excess of \$1,000,000;
>
> \(iii\) Approval of the annual operating budget, if the proposed budget reflects a variance exceeding 10% of the prior year\'s approved budget;
>
> \(iv\) Any single capital expenditure in excess of \$250,000 that is not included in an approved annual budget;
>
> \(v\) The admission of new Members to the Company;
>
> \(vi\) Any amendment to the Operating Agreement;
>
> \(vii\) The dissolution or winding up of the Company;
>
> \(viii\) The commencement of any litigation or arbitration in which the amount in controversy exceeds \$100,000; and
>
> \(ix\) The entry into any agreement or transaction with an Affiliate of the Managing Member, except to the extent such agreement or transaction is on arms\'-length terms and has been disclosed to all Members.

Because GDG holds 72% of the outstanding Membership Interests, and the threshold for Major Decisions is 75%, GDG alone cannot approve any Major Decision. At least one Passive Member must join GDG in approving any Major Decision. Conversely, no combination of the two Passive Members (holding 18% and 10%, respectively, for a combined 28%) can reach the 75% threshold without GDG\'s participation, effectively granting GDG a veto over all Major Decisions.

The list of Major Decisions does not include the filing of a voluntary petition for bankruptcy, insolvency, or reorganization. This decision is not subject to any heightened approval requirement under the Operating Agreement.

**3.3 Officers.** The Operating Agreement provides that the Managing Member may designate one or more officers of the Company. As of the date of this summary, no officers have been formally appointed. Neil Ashford Graydon acts in the capacity of the Company\'s authorized representative through his role as sole member and manager of GDG, the Managing Member. All documents executed on behalf of the Company are executed by Mr. Graydon in his capacity as sole member and manager of GDG.

**3.4 Compensation of Managing Member**

\[Redacted --- Managing Member compensation and fee provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: GDG is entitled to an asset management fee and a development management fee, the terms of which are detailed in the unredacted agreement. Borrower\'s counsel will make the relevant fee provisions available upon request.\]

**[Section 4: Transfer Restrictions]{.underline}**

**4.1 General Restriction on Transfers**

No Member may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, encumber, or otherwise dispose of (collectively, \"**Transfer**\") all or any portion of its Membership Interest in the Company without the prior written consent of the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Membership Interests, calculated by excluding the Transferring Member\'s own interest from the denominator used in determining the 75% threshold. Any Transfer made in violation of this Section 4 shall be void and of no force or effect, and the Company and the remaining Members shall not be obligated to recognize or give effect to any such attempted Transfer. The transfer restrictions in this Section 4 apply exclusively to Transfers of Membership Interests in the Company and do not purport to restrict or address changes in the internal or upstream ownership, management, or control of any Member entity.

**4.2 Permitted Transfers**

Notwithstanding the general restriction set forth in Section 4.1, the following Transfers are designated as \"**Permitted Transfers**\" and do not require the consent of the Managing Member or any other Member:

> \(a\) Transfers by any Member to an Affiliate of such Member, as defined in Section 4.5, provided that the transferee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of the Operating Agreement;
>
> \(b\) Transfers by GDG to any trust established by Neil Ashford Graydon for estate planning purposes, provided that Neil Ashford Graydon retains voting and management control over the transferred Membership Interest during his lifetime;
>
> \(c\) Transfers by Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP directed by its general partner, Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, including transfers to any successor fund managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate thereof, without the consent of any other Member;
>
> \(d\) Transfers among existing Members.

Section 4.2(c) is particularly broad in scope. It grants Tidewater GP Holdings LLC the sole authority to direct Transfers of Tidewater\'s 18% Membership Interest, not only to Affiliates of Tidewater but also to any \"successor fund\" managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC. The term \"successor fund\" is not defined in the Operating Agreement. This provision could result in the Transfer of Tidewater\'s 18% Membership Interest to a fund entity that is under substantially different economic beneficial ownership than Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, so long as Tidewater GP Holdings LLC (or an Affiliate thereof) serves as the manager or general partner of such successor fund. No consent from GDG, Harborline, or any third party is required for such a Transfer.

The Operating Agreement does not contain any provision restricting or requiring consent for changes in the internal ownership, control, or management of any Member at the entity level. By way of illustration:

> • Neil Ashford Graydon could sell or transfer his membership interest in GDG, the 72% Managing Member, to a third party. Because the Membership Interest in the Company would continue to be held in the name of GDG, no Transfer of a Membership Interest in the Company would occur, and the restrictions in Section 4.1 would not be triggered.
>
> • Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, the general partner of Tidewater, could itself be acquired by, merged with, or replaced by a new entity. Such a change would effectively alter who controls the 18% Membership Interest held by Tidewater, but would not constitute a Transfer of a Membership Interest in the Company.
>
> • The internal membership or management of Harborline Capital Advisors LLC could change entirely without triggering the Transfer restrictions, because the Membership Interest in the Company would remain registered in the name of Harborline.

The Operating Agreement contains no \"change of control\" provision that would capture indirect or upstream transfers or that would require notice to, or consent from, the Company or its Members in connection with any such change.

**4.3 Right of First Offer**

If any Member desires to Transfer all or any portion of its Membership Interest other than pursuant to a Permitted Transfer, such Member (the \"**Offering Member**\") must first deliver to the Company and the remaining Members a written offer (the \"**Transfer Notice**\") setting forth the proposed price, terms, and conditions of the proposed Transfer and the identity of the proposed third-party transferee. The remaining Members shall have the right, exercisable within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Transfer Notice, to elect to purchase the offered Membership Interest pro rata in proportion to their respective Membership Interests (excluding the Offering Member\'s interest) at the same price and on the same terms set forth in the Transfer Notice. If the remaining Members decline or fail to exercise their right of first offer within such thirty (30) day period, the Offering Member may consummate the proposed Transfer to the proposed third-party transferee within ninety (90) days of the expiration of the right of first offer period, provided that such Transfer is on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice.

**4.4 Tag-Along and Drag-Along Rights**

\[Redacted --- Tag-along and drag-along provisions summarized as follows: If GDG proposes to Transfer 50% or more of its Membership Interest to a third party, the Passive Members have tag-along rights permitting them to participate in such Transfer on the same price and terms. If Members holding 80% or more of the outstanding Membership Interests approve a sale of the Company or the Property to a third party, they may require all other Members to participate in such sale on the same terms and conditions (drag-along). Detailed mechanics redacted.\]

**4.5 Definition of \"Affiliate\"**

The Operating Agreement defines \"**Affiliate**\" as follows:

> \"with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with, such Person. \'Control\' means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.\"

This is a standard \"control\"-based Affiliate definition. However, the Permitted Transfer provision in Section 4.2(c) extends beyond transfers to Affiliates of Tidewater --- it permits transfers to \"any successor fund managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or any Affiliate thereof.\" A successor fund managed by an Affiliate of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC could be under substantially different ultimate economic ownership than Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP itself, yet such a transfer would qualify as a Permitted Transfer not requiring any consent. The interaction of the Affiliate definition with the Permitted Transfer carve-outs creates a broad pathway for the transfer of Tidewater\'s 18% interest outside the ordinary consent requirements.

**[Section 5: Distributions]{.underline}**

**5.1 Distribution Waterfall**

Distributable Cash Flow, defined as net cash flow from operations after payment of operating expenses, debt service, and required reserves (but before capital expenditures funded from reserves), shall be distributed to the Members in the following order of priority:

> **First**, to all Members, pro rata in accordance with their respective Membership Interests, until each Member has received cumulative distributions under this tier equal to an eight percent (8%) per annum preferred return on such Member\'s unreturned capital contributions (the \"**Preferred Return**\"). The Preferred Return shall accrue and compound annually to the extent not distributed in any given period.
>
> **Second**, to all Members, pro rata in accordance with their respective Membership Interests, until each Member has received cumulative distributions under this tier and all prior tiers equal to one hundred percent (100%) of such Member\'s aggregate capital contributions.
>
> **Third**, thereafter, eighty percent (80%) to GDG and twenty percent (20%) to the Passive Members. The Passive Members\' share of the Third tier shall be allocated among the Passive Members pro rata based on their respective Passive Member Membership Interests (i.e., Tidewater receives 20% × 18/28 ≈ 12.86% and Harborline receives 20% × 10/28 ≈ 7.14%) (the \"**Promote**\").

The Third tier reflect a promote or carried interest structure for GDG, the Managing Member, which is typical in real estate joint venture arrangements.

**5.2 Distributions from Capital Events**

\[Redacted --- Capital event distribution provisions (including distributions from sale, refinancing, condemnation, or casualty proceeds) summarized as follows: Capital event proceeds are distributed in the same waterfall priority as Section 5.1, except that the Third tier promote split is seventy/thirty (70% to GDG and 30% to Passive Members) for capital events. Detailed capital event distribution mechanics, including clawback provisions, are redacted.\]

**5.3 Tax Distributions**

\[Redacted --- The Operating Agreement provides that the Company shall make quarterly tax distributions to the Members in amounts estimated to be sufficient to cover each Member\'s federal and state tax liabilities arising from allocations of Company taxable income for such quarter. Tax distributions are treated as advances against distributions otherwise payable under Section 5.1 and shall reduce amounts otherwise distributable to each recipient Member. Detailed provisions redacted.\]

**[Section 6: Accounting and Reports]{.underline}**

**6.1 Books and Records**

The Managing Member shall maintain, or cause to be maintained, complete and accurate books and records of the Company at the Company\'s principal office located at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401. Each Member and its duly authorized representatives shall have the right to inspect and copy such books and records during normal business hours upon reasonable prior written notice to the Managing Member. The books and records of the Company shall be maintained on the accrual basis of accounting in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied.

**6.2 Financial Reporting**

The Managing Member shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Member the following financial reports:

> \(a\) **Quarterly Financial Statements**: Unaudited quarterly financial statements of the Company, including a balance sheet and statement of income and cash flows, within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter;
>
> \(b\) **Annual Financial Statements**: Annual financial statements of the Company, reviewed (but not audited) by an independent certified public accountant selected by the Managing Member, within ninety (90) days after the end of each fiscal year; and
>
> \(c\) **Schedule K-1s**: IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) for each Member, within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year.

The Operating Agreement requires only \"reviewed\" financial statements on an annual basis --- not audited financial statements. This standard of financial reporting is lower than the audited financial statement requirement that may be imposed by the proposed loan documents.

**6.3 Fiscal Year**

The fiscal year of the Company is the calendar year, commencing January 1 and ending December 31 of each year.

**[Section 7: Exculpation and Indemnification]{.underline}**

\[Redacted --- Exculpation and indemnification provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: The Operating Agreement contains standard provisions exculpating the Managing Member and its Affiliates from liability to the Company or any Member for any act or omission taken in good faith, except for liability arising from fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence. The Operating Agreement further provides for indemnification of the Managing Member and its Affiliates by the Company from Company assets for claims arising out of or relating to the Managing Member\'s service in such capacity, subject to the same carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, and gross negligence.\]

**[Section 8: Dissolution and Winding Up]{.underline}**

**8.1 Events of Dissolution**

The Company shall be dissolved upon the earliest to occur of the following events:

> \(a\) The sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of the Property and the distribution of all net proceeds therefrom to the Members in accordance with Section 5;
>
> \(b\) The prior written consent of Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding Membership Interests;
>
> \(c\) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under S.C. Code Ann. § 33-44-701; or
>
> \(d\) The occurrence of any event that makes it unlawful for the Company to continue its business.

The Operating Agreement does not include any provision requiring the consent of any lender, independent director, independent manager, or other third party as a condition to the voluntary dissolution of the Company. There is no separateness covenant within the dissolution provisions or elsewhere in the Operating Agreement providing that the Company shall not dissolve, liquidate, or wind up its affairs without the prior written consent of the Company\'s secured lender. As noted above, the 75% approval threshold for dissolution under Section 8.1(b) requires GDG\'s participation but does not require unanimous consent of all Members or consent of an independent party.

**8.2 Winding Up**

\[Redacted --- Winding up provisions omitted from this summary. Summary note: Upon dissolution, the Managing Member (or a liquidating trustee appointed by Members holding a majority of the Membership Interests, if GDG is unable or unwilling to serve) shall wind up the Company\'s affairs, liquidate its assets in an orderly manner, discharge or make provision for the Company\'s liabilities to creditors, and distribute remaining assets to the Members in accordance with their positive capital account balances.\]

**[Section 9: Miscellaneous Provisions]{.underline}**

**9.1 Amendments.** The Operating Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding Membership Interests; *provided, however*, that no amendment that would (i) alter the economic rights of any Member, including but not limited to such Member\'s rights under the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 5, or (ii) increase any Member\'s capital contribution obligation beyond amounts previously committed, shall be effective without the prior written consent of each Member so affected. **9.2 Governing Law**

The Operating Agreement is governed by and shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina, without regard to the conflicts of laws principles thereof.

**9.3 Notices.** All notices, demands, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under the Operating Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered by hand, sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service, or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed to the relevant Member at the address set forth in Section 2.1 or at such other address as such Member may designate by written notice to the Company and the other Members. Email notice is permitted for routine business communications but shall not be effective for notices of default, capital calls, or any Major Decision requiring Member approval.

**9.4 Entire Agreement**

The Operating Agreement, together with all exhibits and schedules thereto, constitutes the entire agreement among the Members with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether written or oral, among the Members relating to the Company.

**9.5 Severability.** If any provision of the Operating Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of the Operating Agreement, and the Operating Agreement shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been contained therein.

Summary note: The Operating Agreement contains a mandatory mediation provision, requiring the Members to submit any dispute arising under the Operating Agreement to mediation in Charleston, South Carolina, prior to initiating any other form of dispute resolution. If mediation is unsuccessful, the dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration in Charleston, South Carolina, administered under the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. **[PHASE I ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT]{.underline}**

**[EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

**Prepared in Accordance with ASTM E1527-21**

**Report Number:** CLR-2025-0119

**Date of Report:** January 28, 2025

**Subject Property:** 520--534 King Street Charleston, South Carolina 29403

**Prepared for: Calverley Heritage Bank 412 Whitaker Street Savannah, Georgia 31401**

Attention: Marcus Prideaux, Senior Vice President -- Commercial Real Estate Lending

**Additional User / Intended Reliance Party:** Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC 88 Broad Street, Suite 200 Charleston, South Carolina 29401

**Prepared by:** Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC 445 Rivers Avenue, Suite 300 North Charleston, South Carolina 29405

**NOTICE:** This Executive Summary is extracted from the full Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Report No. CLR-2025-0119 dated January 28, 2025. The full report, including all appendices (regulatory database search results, historical aerial photographs, Sanborn fire insurance maps, site photographs, interview records, and the assessor\'s qualifications), should be reviewed in its entirety for a complete understanding of the assessment findings and their basis. This Executive Summary alone does not constitute a complete Phase I Environmental Site Assessment under ASTM E1527-21 or 40 CFR Part 312.

**[1. Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**

Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC (\"Clearfield\") was retained by Calverley Heritage Bank (\"CHB\" or \"User\") to conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") of the property located at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403 (the \"Subject Property\"). The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to identify Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"RECs\"), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") in connection with the Subject Property, as those terms are defined in ASTM E1527-21, Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process.

This assessment was conducted to support a proposed commercial real estate loan from Calverley Heritage Bank to Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC in connection with the acquisition and renovation of the Subject Property. Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC has been designated as an additional user of and intended reliance party for this report with the prior written consent of Clearfield.

The Phase I ESA was conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 and is intended to satisfy the \"All Appropriate Inquiries\" (\"AAI\") standard under 40 CFR Part 312, thereby qualifying the User for the innocent landowner, contiguous property owner, and bona fide prospective purchaser defenses to liability under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. §§ 9601 *et seq.*

The scope of services performed in connection with this Phase I ESA included the following:

> • Review of federal, state, tribal, and local environmental regulatory database records, including standard and additional databases as specified by ASTM E1527-21;
>
> • Historical use review utilizing aerial photographs (reviewed from 1938 to present), Sanborn fire insurance maps, city directories, and building department records obtained from the City of Charleston Department of Planning, Preservation and Sustainability;
>
> • Site reconnaissance, conducted on January 15, 2025, including an interior and exterior inspection of the Subject Property and visual observation of adjoining properties from the Subject Property boundaries;
>
> • Interviews with the current property owner, current occupants, and local government officials with knowledge of the Subject Property and surrounding area; and
>
> • Evaluation of adjoining and nearby properties for conditions that may affect the Subject Property.

**Limitations:** This assessment did not include the sampling or analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, or building materials. No Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (subsurface investigation) was conducted as part of this engagement. The findings and conclusions set forth herein are based solely on non-invasive methods.

**Data Gaps:** No significant data gaps were identified during the course of this assessment. Historical records were available for the Subject Property from 1938 to the present, and regulatory database searches returned complete results for all standard search distances.

**[2. Subject Property Description]{.underline}**

**Address:** 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403

**Legal Description:** Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the Register of Mesne Conveyances (\"RMC\") Office for Charleston County, South Carolina; together with that certain strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed to the predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**Tax Map Numbers:** 460-12-04-007 (Lot 7), 460-12-04-008 (Lot 8), and 460-12-04-009 (Lot 9)

**Total Land Area:** Approximately 0.38 acres (approximately 16,553 square feet)

**Improvements:** The Subject Property is improved with a mixed-use commercial building consisting of ground-floor retail space (three bays totaling approximately 11,400 square feet) and upper-floor office space (two stories, approximately 19,600 square feet), for a total gross building area of approximately 31,000 square feet. The building features a masonry and steel-frame construction with a flat membrane roof, which was last replaced in 2017 according to building department records.

**Year Built:** The original commercial structure was constructed in 1952. A significant renovation was completed in 2004, converting the upper floors from storage and warehouse use to Class B office space and upgrading building systems including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire suppression.

**Current Use:** Mixed-use retail and office, as follows:

> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 1** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 7): Occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc., a specialty grocery retailer.
>
> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 2** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 8): Currently vacant.
>
> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 3** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 9): Occupied by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC, an interior design firm.
>
> • **Second Floor --- Suite A** (approximately 9,800 SF): Occupied by Tidemark Consulting Group LLC, a management consulting firm.
>
> • **Second Floor --- Suite B** (approximately 9,800 SF): Currently vacant.

**Physical Description of Lots:** Lot 7 is the southwestern parcel, fronting King Street, containing Bay 1 on the ground floor and a portion of the second-floor area. Lot 8 is the central parcel containing Bay 2 and additional second-floor area. Lot 9 is the northeastern parcel containing Bay 3 and the remainder of the second floor. The former Anson Lane strip runs along the rear (northwest) boundary of Lots 7, 8, and 9 and currently provides rear access and loading for the building.

**Zoning:** GB (General Business), City of Charleston.

**Topography:** The Subject Property is generally flat with minimal grade change across the site. The Subject Property is situated in FEMA Flood Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) based on FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map Panel No. 45019C0520J, effective December 4, 2020.

**Utilities:** Public water and sewer service is provided by the Charleston Water System. Electrical service is provided by South Carolina Electric & Gas. An easement for underground utility lines across the rear of the Subject Property is recorded in Deed Book 987 at Page 112, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**[3. Historical Use Summary]{.underline}**

The following historical use summary is based on Clearfield\'s review of Sanborn fire insurance maps (1902, 1919, 1944, 1955, 1970, and 1989 editions), aerial photographs (reviewed at approximately five-year intervals from 1938 to present), city directories (1948 through 2024), and building department records obtained from the City of Charleston.

**Subject Property Historical Uses:**

**Pre-1952:** The Subject Property was part of the Hampstead Village residential neighborhood. Lots 7, 8, and 9 were each improved with single-family wood-frame residences, consistent with the surrounding residential character of the area as depicted on Sanborn maps and aerial photographs from this period. Anson Lane was a public alley running behind the lots, providing rear access to the residences and adjacent properties.

**1952:** The single-family residences on Lots 7, 8, and 9 were demolished and the original commercial structure was constructed across all three lots. Building department records indicate the structure was initially built for general retail purposes. The 1955 Sanborn map depicts the building as a one-story commercial structure with a partial second-story storage area.

**1952--2003:** The Subject Property was in continuous use for general retail and small commercial office purposes. City directory listings and building department records from this period identify various tenants, including a hardware store (approximately 1956--1971), a clothing retailer (approximately 1972--1989), and miscellaneous small office and retail tenants thereafter. No evidence of hazardous substance use, storage, treatment, or disposal on the Subject Property was identified during this period. No underground storage tanks or above-ground storage tanks were identified in association with any tenant or use during this period.

**2004:** A significant renovation converted the upper floors from storage and warehouse use to Class B office space. Building systems, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire suppression, were upgraded. Building department permits and inspection records from the 2004 renovation do not reference any environmental incidents, the discovery of contaminated materials, or the removal of underground storage tanks.

**2019:** City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 vacated the public alley formerly known as Anson Lane. The vacated strip was conveyed to the then-owner of the Subject Property by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**2004--Present:** The Subject Property has been in continuous mixed-use retail and office occupancy, consistent with its current configuration.

**Adjacent Property Historical Use --- 518 King Street:**

The property located at 518 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina (immediately southwest of and adjoining Lot 7 of the Subject Property) is of particular significance to this assessment. Based on city directory listings, building department records, and Sanborn map review, 518 King Street was historically operated as a dry cleaning establishment known as \"King Street Cleaners\" from approximately 1968 through 2005. Dry cleaning operations at this location involved the use of perchloroethylene (\"PCE,\" also known as tetrachloroethylene) and other petroleum-based solvents. The dry cleaning facility was closed in 2005, and the building at 518 King Street was subsequently converted to a restaurant, which remains its current use. Environmental contamination associated with the former dry cleaning operation at 518 King Street is discussed in detail in Section 5 below.

**[4. Findings --- Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)]{.underline}**

**No Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs) were identified in connection with the Subject Property.**

Clearfield reviewed applicable federal and state environmental regulatory databases in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 search distance requirements, including: the EPA National Priorities List (\"NPL\"); the CERCLIS/SEMS database; the RCRA Corrective Action (CORRACTS) and Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF) lists; the RCRA generators lists (large and small quantity generators); the Emergency Response Notification System (\"ERNS\"); state-equivalent hazardous waste site and solid waste facility lists; the Leaking Underground Storage Tank (\"LUST\") and Underground Storage Tank (\"UST\") databases maintained by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (\"SCDHEC\"); SCDHEC Voluntary Cleanup Program records; SCDHEC Brownfields Program sites; and state spill and release notification databases.

The Subject Property does not appear on any federal or state environmental database as a site of concern, listed facility, generator, or location of a reported release.

During the site reconnaissance conducted on January 15, 2025, no evidence of underground storage tanks, above-ground storage tanks, or hazardous substance storage was observed on the Subject Property or identified in historical records. No evidence of staining, stressed vegetation, illegal dumping, waste disposal, or other indicators of releases or threatened releases of hazardous substances or petroleum products was observed on the Subject Property.

**No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs) were identified in connection with the Subject Property.**

**One (1) Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) was identified in connection with the Subject Property**, as described in detail in Section 5 below.

**[5. Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) --- Lot 7]{.underline}**

**5.1 Background and Source of Contamination**

A Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (\"CREC\"), as defined by ASTM E1527-21, was identified with respect to Lot 7 of the Subject Property (Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007). A CREC is defined under ASTM E1527-21 as a recognized environmental condition resulting from a past release of hazardous substances or petroleum products that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority, with hazardous substances or petroleum products allowed to remain in place subject to the implementation of required controls.

The CREC arises from off-site contamination originating at the adjacent property located at 518 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, which is immediately southwest of and adjoining Lot 7. As described in Section 3 above, 518 King Street was formerly operated as \"King Street Cleaners,\" a dry cleaning establishment, from approximately 1968 to 2005.

Operations at King Street Cleaners involved the use of perchloroethylene (\"PCE,\" also known as tetrachloroethylene) and petroleum-based solvents in commercial dry cleaning equipment. A release of PCE and petroleum-based solvents from the former dry cleaning operation resulted in subsurface soil and shallow groundwater contamination that migrated off-site in a generally northeastern direction --- consistent with the local shallow groundwater flow gradient --- toward and into the southwest corner of Lot 7 of the Subject Property.

The contamination was identified, reported to the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (\"SCDHEC\"), and assigned SCDHEC Site Identification Number SC-29403-0772. The SCDHEC file for this site documents the nature and extent of contamination, the remediation activities undertaken, and the regulatory determination described below.

**5.2 Remediation and Regulatory Closure**

Remediation activities were conducted at the source area on the 518 King Street property and at the impacted portion of Lot 7 of the Subject Property under SCDHEC oversight. Remediation included excavation and off-site disposal of impacted soils, in-situ chemical oxidation treatment of residual soil and groundwater contamination, and a multi-year program of groundwater and soil vapor monitoring to assess the effectiveness of remedial activities.

Following the completion of remedial activities and a period of post-remediation monitoring demonstrating stable or declining contaminant concentrations, SCDHEC issued a \"No Further Action\" (\"NFA\") letter dated August 12, 2021, for SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772. The NFA letter concluded that residual contamination levels in soil and groundwater at and beneath the southwest corner of Lot 7 had been reduced to levels protective of human health and the environment under a commercial and non-residential use scenario, subject to certain institutional controls.

**Important:** The NFA letter was issued subject to conditions --- specifically, the implementation and maintenance of the institutional controls described in Section 5.3 below. The NFA status is contingent upon continued compliance with these institutional controls. A failure to maintain the required institutional controls could result in SCDHEC reopening the site for additional investigation, remediation, or regulatory action.

**5.3 Institutional Controls --- Recorded Land Use Restriction**

As a condition of the SCDHEC NFA determination for Site ID SC-29403-0772, a Land Use Restriction (\"LUR\") was recorded against Lot 7 of the Subject Property in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, at Deed Book 1203 at Page 89. The recorded LUR imposes two specific obligations that run with the land and are binding upon all current and future owners, tenants, lessees, successors, and assigns of Lot 7:

> **(a) Prohibition on Residential Use.** The ground floor of Lot 7 --- that is, Bay 1 of the Subject Property, comprising approximately 3,800 square feet and currently occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery --- shall not be converted to or used for residential purposes. This restriction is intended to prevent exposure pathways associated with continuous residential indoor occupancy, including potential vapor intrusion of residual volatile organic compounds (\"VOCs\") from subsurface soil and groundwater into the indoor air of Bay 1 at levels that may exceed residential screening criteria.
>
> **(b) Vapor Barrier Maintenance Obligation.** The property owner is required to maintain, in good condition and working order, a vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1 (Lot 7, ground floor). The vapor barrier was installed during remediation activities to mitigate the potential for vapor intrusion of residual VOCs --- principally PCE and its degradation products --- from subsurface soil and groundwater into the indoor air of Bay 1. The LUR requires that the vapor barrier not be penetrated, removed, or compromised without prior written approval from SCDHEC. Any renovation, construction, demolition, or alteration activity affecting the floor slab of Bay 1 must include inspection and, if necessary, repair or replacement of the vapor barrier, with prior written notification to SCDHEC.

The LUR is binding upon all current and future owners, tenants, and successors in interest to Lot 7 and constitutes a covenant running with the land enforceable by SCDHEC.

During the site reconnaissance conducted on January 15, 2025, Clearfield observed that the ground floor of Bay 1 is currently occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery retailer. This use is consistent with the commercial-use restriction imposed by the LUR. No evidence of vapor barrier damage, slab penetrations, or other conditions suggesting a compromise of the vapor barrier was observed during the site reconnaissance. However, because the vapor barrier is installed beneath the concrete slab, it was not directly visible or inspectable during the reconnaissance. Clearfield recommends that any prospective purchaser confirm the integrity of the vapor barrier through a qualified inspection conducted by a licensed environmental professional prior to or promptly after acquisition, and particularly before any renovation activity affecting the Bay 1 floor slab.

**5.4 Implications for the Subject Property**

The CREC does not constitute a Recognized Environmental Condition because the contamination has been addressed to the satisfaction of SCDHEC and the site has received an NFA letter. However, the CREC classification under ASTM E1527-21 reflects the fact that residual contamination remains in place at levels that exceed unrestricted use standards and that the continued effectiveness of the institutional controls (the recorded LUR) is necessary for the site to remain protective of human health.

If the institutional controls are not maintained --- for example, if the vapor barrier is breached or rendered ineffective during renovation or construction activities, or if the ground floor of Bay 1 is converted to residential use in violation of the LUR --- the NFA status could be jeopardized. Such a breach could result in SCDHEC requiring additional subsurface investigation, remediation measures, or other regulatory action at the expense of the then-current property owner.

The CREC and associated LUR are matters of public record filed with the RMC Office for Charleston County. Clearfield understands from the preliminary title commitment issued for this transaction (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC) that the LUR recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89 is listed as a Schedule B-II exception to title. Any lender, purchaser, or other party relying on this report should review the recorded LUR in its entirety and consult with legal counsel regarding its implications.

**Note Regarding Planned Renovation:** Clearfield understands from discussions with representatives of Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC that the prospective purchaser intends to undertake a renovation of the Subject Property that may include HVAC system replacement, elevator modernization, and façade restoration. If any renovation activities involve penetration of, alteration to, or work in proximity to the Bay 1 floor slab on Lot 7, care must be taken to avoid compromising the vapor barrier installed beneath the slab. Clearfield recommends that the renovation contractor be made aware of the existence and location of the vapor barrier and of the LUR requirements, and that SCDHEC be notified in writing in advance of any work affecting the Bay 1 slab. Failure to observe these precautions could result in a violation of the LUR and a reopening of the SCDHEC site file, with attendant regulatory and financial consequences for the property owner and, potentially, the lender.

**[6. Phase II Recommendation]{.underline}**

Based on the findings of this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Clearfield does **not** recommend a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (subsurface investigation) for the Subject Property at this time.

The sole environmental finding identified in this assessment --- the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition on Lot 7 --- relates to contamination that has been addressed through SCDHEC-supervised remediation and for which an NFA letter has been issued (August 12, 2021, SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772). Residual contamination is managed through recorded institutional controls in the form of the Land Use Restriction recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89. No conditions were observed during the site reconnaissance or identified during the records review that would suggest a change in subsurface conditions or a failure of the institutional controls. Accordingly, no additional subsurface investigation is warranted at this time unless the institutional controls are breached or new information comes to light suggesting a material change in subsurface conditions.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Clearfield recommends the following actions in connection with the proposed transaction:

> \(a\) The prospective purchaser and borrower (Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC) should obtain and review a complete copy of the SCDHEC remediation file for Site ID SC-29403-0772, including all sampling data, remediation reports, groundwater monitoring results, and the NFA letter with all conditions and attachments.
>
> \(b\) The integrity of the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 floor slab should be confirmed through a qualified inspection by a licensed environmental professional prior to or promptly following acquisition of the Subject Property.
>
> \(c\) Any renovation contractor performing work in or near Bay 1 on Lot 7 should be informed of the existence and location of the vapor barrier and of the requirements of the recorded LUR, and SCDHEC should be notified in writing in advance of any work affecting the Bay 1 floor slab.
>
> \(d\) The lender (Calverley Heritage Bank) should consider requiring the borrower to maintain ongoing compliance with the LUR as a specific covenant in the loan documents, including provisions addressing the consequences of non-compliance and the lender\'s remedies in the event of a breach of the institutional controls.

**Note: Calverley Heritage Bank has waived the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment requirement for this transaction based on the CREC status, the issuance of the SCDHEC NFA letter, and the existence of the recorded institutional controls. This waiver is documented in correspondence dated January 22, 2025, between Marcus Prideaux, Senior Vice President -- Commercial Real Estate Lending, Calverley Heritage Bank, and Clearfield.**

**[7. Conclusions and Opinion]{.underline}**

Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC has performed a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment of the Subject Property located at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403, in conformance with the scope and limitations of ASTM E1527-21, *Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process*.

The following is a summary of findings:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Condition**                                            **Finding**
  -------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)               None identified

  Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)   One (1) identified --- petroleum and solvent contamination (principally PCE) from former dry cleaning operation at adjacent 518 King Street, migrating to southwest corner of Lot 7; remediated under SCDHEC oversight; NFA letter issued August 12, 2021 (SCDHEC Site ID: SC-29403-0772); subject to recorded Land Use Restriction (Deed Book 1203, Page 89, RMC Office for Charleston County) requiring maintenance of vapor barrier beneath Bay 1 floor slab and prohibiting residential use of ground floor of Lot 7

  Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)   None identified

  De Minimis Conditions                                    None identified

  Significant Data Gaps                                    None identified
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the professional opinion of Clearfield, the Subject Property is suitable for the proposed acquisition and continued commercial use, provided that the institutional controls associated with the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition on Lot 7 are maintained in full compliance with SCDHEC requirements and the terms of the recorded Land Use Restriction. Any future change of use, renovation, or alteration affecting the Bay 1 floor slab on Lot 7 should be undertaken with due regard for the vapor barrier and the LUR, as described in Sections 5 and 6 of this Executive Summary and in greater detail in the full Phase I ESA report.

**[8. Qualifications and Limitations]{.underline}**

This Executive Summary is a condensed extract of the full Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025. The full report, including all appendices --- specifically, Appendix A (Regulatory Database Search Results), Appendix B (Historical Aerial Photographs), Appendix C (Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps), Appendix D (Site Photographs), Appendix E (Interview Records), and Appendix F (Environmental Professional Qualifications) --- should be reviewed in its entirety for a complete understanding of the assessment findings and their basis. This Executive Summary does not replace or supersede the full report.

This assessment was performed for the exclusive use of the identified User (Calverley Heritage Bank) and the additional reliance party (Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC). No other party may rely on this report or this Executive Summary without the prior written consent of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Any unauthorized use or reliance is at the sole risk of the unauthorized party.

The assessment reflects conditions observed and information available as of the date of the site reconnaissance (January 15, 2025) and the date of the report (January 28, 2025). Environmental conditions may change over time due to natural processes, human activities, changes in regulatory standards, or other factors. Clearfield assumes no obligation to update this report and no responsibility for changes in conditions or information that occur after the date of this report.

This assessment involved no invasive investigation, sampling, testing, or analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, or building materials. The conclusions are based solely on non-invasive methods, including visual observation, records review, and interviews. The presence or absence of hazardous substances or petroleum products in environmental media cannot be confirmed without sampling and laboratory analysis.

The findings and conclusions of this assessment are subject to the inherent limitations of the ASTM E1527-21 standard, including limitations associated with the accuracy and completeness of historical records, the reliability of regulatory database information, the scope of visual observations, and the potential for conditions that are not identifiable through non-invasive methods. No Phase I ESA can wholly eliminate uncertainty regarding the potential for recognized environmental conditions in connection with a property.

This assessment was conducted under the supervision and direction of Dr. Rebecca Stanton, P.G., a Licensed Geologist in the State of South Carolina (Registration No. 1847), who serves as a Senior Environmental Scientist and Principal of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Dr. Stanton meets the qualifications of an \"Environmental Professional\" as defined in ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.26, and 40 CFR § 312.10, by reason of education, training, and experience in environmental site assessment.

## 1. Executive Summary

**Property Identification:** 520--534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403; Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009.

**Property Type:** Mixed-use --- ground-floor retail (three bays, 11,400 SF) and upper-floor office (two stories, 19,600 SF); total gross building area of 31,000 SF.

**Land Area:** 0.38 acres (approximately 16,553 SF).

**Zoning:** GB (General Business), City of Charleston.

**Extraordinary Assumptions:** (1) The as-stabilized value assumes completion of the planned \$3,150,000 renovation program within 14 months and lease-up of currently vacant space to 95% occupancy within 24 months from the effective date. (2) No extraordinary assumptions have been made regarding environmental conditions; the property is subject to a recorded land use restriction on Lot 7 (see Section 5).

**Hypothetical Conditions:** The as-stabilized value is based on the hypothetical condition that renovation is complete and the property achieves stabilized occupancy. This is a prospective value estimate as of the anticipated stabilization date, estimated to be Q1 2027.

## 2. Property Description

### 2.1 Site Description

**Location.** The subject property is located in the Upper King Street corridor of Charleston, South Carolina --- a commercially vibrant mixed-use district with strong retail, restaurant, and office demand. The immediate neighborhood is characterized by a mix of adaptive-reuse commercial buildings, boutique retail, creative office tenants, and nationally branded restaurants, all supported by robust pedestrian traffic and tourism.

**Legal Description.** Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina; together with a strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed to the predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443.

**Land Area.** 0.38 acres, approximately 16,553 SF, consisting of three contiguous tax parcels (Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009) plus the vacated Anson Lane right-of-way.

**Shape, Topography, and Frontage.** The assemblage is generally rectangular with level topography and approximately 120 linear feet of frontage on King Street, a major north-south commercial arterial providing direct vehicular and pedestrian access.

**Zoning.** GB (General Business), City of Charleston --- permits retail, office, restaurant, and mixed uses by right. Residential use above the ground floor is permitted. Ground-floor residential use on Lot 7 is restricted by a recorded land use restriction (see Section 5).

**Utilities.** All public utilities are available, including municipal water and sewer, electric service, natural gas, and telecommunications.

**Easements and Encumbrances.** An easement in favor of South Carolina Electric & Gas for underground utility lines, recorded in Deed Book 987 at Page 112, is a standard utility easement that does not materially affect the property's use or value. Additionally, a decorative iron balcony, characteristic of Charleston's historic architectural vernacular, extends approximately 2.5 feet beyond the front building wall over the King Street public right-of-way. The encroachment is reflected as a Schedule B-II exception on the title commitment. The appraiser has treated this as a minor physical consideration that does not materially impair the property's marketability or value, noting that such balcony encroachments are common in Charleston's historic commercial districts and are typically permitted by the City of Charleston under encroachment licenses. However, the existence of the encroachment may require maintenance of a valid encroachment permit, and any city-mandated removal could affect the historic façade. The lender is advised to confirm the status of the encroachment permit in consultation with legal counsel.

**FEMA Flood Zone.** Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard), FEMA Community Panel No. 45019C0418J, effective November 4, 2014. No mandatory flood insurance requirement under federal regulation applies to this property.

### 2.2 Improvements Description

**Year Built / Renovated.** Original structure constructed in 1952; significant renovation completed in 2004.

**Construction.** Masonry and steel frame with brick exterior and stucco detailing; flat roof with a single-ply membrane system.

**Gross Building Area.** 31,000 SF total, configured as follows: Ground Floor --- three retail bays (Bays 1, 2, and 3), each approximately 3,800 SF (11,400 SF total); Upper Floors --- two office stories above grade containing Suite A (9,800 SF) and Suite B (9,800 SF), totaling 19,600 SF. The building is three stories in height.

**Parking.** Limited on-site parking. Tenants and visitors rely on metered street parking and a municipal parking garage located within two blocks.

**Elevator.** One passenger elevator serves all three floors. The elevator has been identified for modernization as part of the renovation budget (\$475,000).

**HVAC.** Central heating and cooling system is nearing the end of its useful life and has been identified for full replacement in the renovation budget (\$1,200,000).

**Overall Condition.** Fair to good. Deferred maintenance is noted in the HVAC system, elevator, and portions of the exterior façade. The borrower's renovation budget of \$3,150,000 addresses these items as follows: HVAC replacement --- \$1,200,000; elevator modernization --- \$475,000; façade restoration (including the decorative iron balcony on the King Street elevation) --- \$625,000; tenant improvement allowances for vacant spaces --- \$550,000; soft costs and contingency --- \$300,000. If city-mandated removal of the encroaching balcony were ever required, additional façade work beyond the current budgeted scope could be necessary.

**ADA Compliance.** Generally compliant. The elevator modernization will bring vertical circulation into conformity with current code requirements.

## 3. Tenant and Lease Summary

### 3.1 Rent Roll and Occupancy
