Total occupied area is 21,400 SF (68%); vacant area is 13,600 SF (32%), comprising Bay 2 (3,800 SF) and Suite B (9,800 SF). The weighted average in-place rent for occupied space is \$19.40/SF (blended across retail and office). Lowcountry Provisions is a local specialty grocer with stable operations and consistent foot traffic. Harmon & Wren is a boutique interior design studio. Tidemark Consulting Group is the largest tenant by both area and rental income, providing anchor cash flow through its lease term expiring March 31, 2029.

### 3.2 Lease Analysis and Notable Provisions

**Lowcountry Provisions Inc. (Bay 1).** NNN lease at \$28.50/SF through December 31, 2027. The tenant is responsible for its pro rata share of operating expenses including real estate taxes, insurance, and common area maintenance. The appraiser notes that this lease does not contain an assignment or subletting consent clause; the appraiser does not opine on the legal implications of this omission but notes it is unusual for a lease of this type.

**Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC (Bay 3).** Modified gross lease at \$24.00/SF through June 30, 2026. The near-term expiration of this lease --- approximately 16 months from the effective date of value --- is a leasing risk factor. Additionally, the Harmon & Wren lease includes a right of first refusal ("ROFR") on the adjacent Bay 2, which is currently vacant. The existence of this ROFR may constrain the borrower's ability to lease Bay 2 to a third-party tenant at optimal market terms, as any bona fide third-party offer must first be presented to Harmon & Wren on matching terms. In the appraiser's as-stabilized projections, this ROFR has been factored into the lease-up timeline for Bay 2, adding an estimated 60--90 days to the projected absorption period to account for the ROFR exercise or waiver process. This ROFR should be considered in any lease-up covenant or stabilization timeline imposed by the lender.

**Tidemark Consulting Group LLC (Suite A).** NNN lease at \$22.00/SF through March 31, 2029. This is the longest remaining lease term among all tenants and provides stable, predictable cash flow through the anticipated loan maturity period.

**Bay 2 (Vacant).** 3,800 SF ground-floor retail; subject to the Harmon & Wren ROFR. Market rent is estimated at \$26.00--\$28.00/SF NNN based on comparable ground-floor retail leases on Upper King Street.

**Suite B (Vacant).** 9,800 SF second-floor office. Market rent is estimated at \$20.00--\$23.00/SF NNN based on comparable Class B office leases in the Charleston CBD and Upper King corridor.

## 4. Market Analysis

**Submarket Overview.** Upper King Street is one of Charleston's premier mixed-use corridors, benefiting from strong pedestrian traffic, growing restaurant and retail demand, tourism, population in-migration, and proximity to the College of Charleston and MUSC employment centers.

**Retail Market.** Ground-floor retail vacancy on Upper King Street is approximately 5--8%. Asking rents range from \$24.00 to \$32.00/SF NNN depending on frontage quality and condition. The subject's ground-floor retail rents are within the prevailing market range.

**Office Market.** Charleston CBD and Upper King office vacancy is approximately 12--15%. Class B office asking rents are \$19.00--\$25.00/SF. The subject's office rents are slightly below the top of the range, which may facilitate lease-up of Suite B.

**Comparable Sales (Summary):**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Sale   Address                SF       Sale Date   Price          Price/SF   Occupancy
  ------ ---------------------- -------- ----------- -------------- ---------- -----------
  1      610 King Street        22,000   Oct. 2024   \$13,200,000   \$600      85%

  2      445 Meeting Street     28,500   Jun. 2024   \$15,675,000   \$550      92%

  3      312--318 King Street   18,700   Jan. 2025   \$11,594,000   \$620      78%
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The subject's implied as-is price of \$587/SF (\$18,200,000 ÷ 31,000 SF) is consistent with the comparable range. The as-stabilized price of \$758/SF (\$23,500,000 ÷ 31,000 SF) reflects a premium justified by completed renovation and stabilized occupancy.

**Capitalization Rates.** Market cap rates for comparable mixed-use properties range from 5.75% to 6.50%. The appraiser selected a going-in cap rate of 6.25% for the as-is valuation (reflecting lease-up risk and deferred maintenance) and 5.85% for the as-stabilized valuation (reflecting reduced risk upon stabilization).

## 5. Environmental and Physical Considerations

**Phase I ESA Reference.** Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025.

**Environmental Findings.** No Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs) were identified. One Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) was identified on Lot 7: a historical petroleum release from a former dry-cleaning operation at the adjacent property (518 King Street) resulted in soil contamination migrating to the southwest corner of Lot 7. The contamination was remediated under South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (SCDHEC) oversight and received a "No Further Action" (NFA) letter dated August 12, 2021 (SCDHEC Site ID: SC-29403-0772). A recorded land use restriction (LUR) is associated with the CREC, recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, Charleston County RMC. The LUR (a) prohibits residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1) and (b) requires maintenance of a vapor barrier beneath the slab of Bay 1.

**Appraiser's Treatment.** The appraiser has considered the CREC and associated land use restriction in the valuation. Because Bay 1 is currently leased to Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery --- a commercial use consistent with the LUR --- and because the NFA letter confirms that no further remediation is required, the appraiser has not applied a value reduction for the CREC. However, the LUR runs with the land, and any future conversion of Bay 1's ground floor to residential use would violate the restriction. The appraiser notes that the zoning (GB --- General Business) and highest and best use analysis support continued commercial use, so the restriction does not currently constrain the property's value. The ongoing obligation to maintain the vapor barrier beneath Bay 1 is a compliance requirement that should be addressed in loan documentation.

**Flood Zone.** FEMA Zone X --- minimal flood hazard. No base flood elevation is applicable and no federally mandated flood insurance is required.

**Balcony Encroachment.** As described in Section 2.1, the approximately 2.5-foot decorative iron balcony encroachment over the King Street right-of-way is characterized as a minor physical consideration consistent with Charleston's historic commercial district character. The appraiser does not consider this encroachment to have a measurable adverse impact on the property's market value, given the prevalence of such features in the Charleston market and the general acceptance by the City of Charleston through encroachment permits. However, the appraiser recommends that the lender confirm the existence of a valid encroachment permit or license and evaluate the risk of city-mandated removal in consultation with legal counsel.

## 6. Valuation Analysis

### 6.1 Highest and Best Use

**As Vacant.** Mixed-use commercial development consistent with GB zoning --- retail on the ground floor and office on upper floors. The site's King Street frontage, location, and zoning support this conclusion.

**As Improved.** Continued use as a mixed-use retail and office building. Renovation to address deferred maintenance will maximize value. The CREC/LUR on Lot 7 restricts ground-floor residential conversion but does not impair commercial highest and best use. The current improvements represent a reasonable and appropriate use of the site; renovation is financially feasible and maximizes the property's value.

### 6.2 Income Capitalization Approach --- As-Is Value

**Potential Gross Income (PGI):**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Component                               Calculation             Amount
  --------------------------------------- ----------------------- --------------------
  In-place rent (occupied spaces)         Per rent roll           \$415,100

  Market rent --- Bay 2                   3,800 SF × \$27.00/SF   \$102,600

  Market rent --- Suite B                 9,800 SF × \$21.50/SF   \$210,700

  **Total PGI at Stabilized Occupancy**                           **\$728,400**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Vacancy and Collection Loss (As-Is).** Current physical vacancy stands at 32%. For occupied spaces, a market-based general vacancy and credit loss allowance of 5% has been applied. After adjustment for current vacancy and credit loss, effective gross income reflects the property's present leasing profile.

**Operating Expenses.** For NNN tenants (Lowcountry Provisions and Tidemark Consulting), most operating expenses are passed through to the tenants. For the modified gross tenant (Harmon & Wren), the landlord bears certain expenses. Estimated total landlord operating expenses --- including management fees, structural reserves, and non-recoverable costs --- are approximately \$85,000 to \$95,000 per year at current occupancy.

**As-Is Net Operating Income.** Approximately \$332,000 to \$345,000, reflecting current 68% occupancy and actual in-place lease terms net of landlord expenses.

**Capitalization Rate.** 6.25% direct capitalization, reflecting lease-up risk, deferred maintenance, and below-stabilized occupancy. The appraiser also performed a discounted cash flow analysis incorporating a projected lease-up and renovation schedule over a 10-year holding period, which supported a value conclusion consistent with the direct capitalization result when reconciled with the property's near-term value-add potential and the \$17,800,000 contract purchase price.

**Value Indication --- As-Is.** The appraiser has reconciled the income capitalization approach with the sales comparison approach and cost approach (not detailed in this summary) to arrive at a final as-is value opinion of **\$18,200,000** as of February 14, 2025.

### 6.3 Income Capitalization Approach --- As-Stabilized Value

**Assumptions.** Renovation completed per the \$3,150,000 budget; stabilized occupancy of 95% achieved; Bay 2 leased at approximately \$27.00/SF NNN; Suite B leased at approximately \$21.50/SF NNN. The estimated lease-up period is 18--24 months from the effective date to achieve 95% occupancy.

The appraiser notes that the right of first refusal held by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC on Bay 2 may extend the lease-up period for that space. Any third-party lease offer for Bay 2 must be submitted to Harmon & Wren under matching terms before it can be executed. This ROFR process is estimated to add 60 to 90 days to the Bay 2 absorption timeline. The lender should consider this constraint when establishing lease-up benchmarks or leasing covenants.

**Stabilized Income:**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Component                           Amount
  ----------------------------------- ------------------------------
  Stabilized PGI                      \$728,400

  Less: Vacancy/Credit Loss (5%)      (\$36,420)

  Stabilized Effective Gross Income   \$691,980

  Less: Operating Expenses            (\$100,000--\$110,000)

  **Stabilized NOI**                  **\$582,000--\$592,000**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------

**Capitalization Rate (As-Stabilized).** 5.85%, reflecting reduced risk upon stabilization, completed renovation, and a stronger occupancy profile.

**Value Indication --- As-Stabilized.** Reconciled to **\$23,500,000**. This value is predicated on the hypothetical condition that renovation is complete and the property achieves 95% stabilized occupancy. It is a prospective value estimate as of the anticipated stabilization date, estimated to be Q1 2027.

## 7. Reconciliation and Final Value Opinions

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Valuation Scenario               Value Opinion      Effective Date               Basis
  -------------------------------- ------------------ ---------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **As-Is Market Value**           **\$18,200,000**   February 14, 2025            Fee simple, subject to existing leases, current physical condition, and current occupancy (68%)

  **As-Stabilized Market Value**   **\$23,500,000**   Prospective (est. Q1 2027)   Fee simple, subject to hypothetical condition of completed renovation and 95% stabilized occupancy
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The as-is value reflects the property's current condition, including deferred maintenance items (aging HVAC system, elevator requiring modernization, façade in need of restoration) and below-stabilized occupancy. The property benefits from a strong King Street location, a creditworthy anchor tenant (Tidemark Consulting Group LLC), and favorable market fundamentals in the Upper King Street submarket. The spread between the as-is and as-stabilized values (\$5,300,000) represents the value-creation opportunity from the planned renovation and lease-up program. The purchase price of \$17,800,000 is below the as-is appraised value of \$18,200,000, suggesting a reasonable acquisition basis.

**Key Ratios for Lender Reference:**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Ratio                  Calculation                   Result
  ---------------------- ----------------------------- --------------------
  Proposed Loan Amount                                 \$14,750,000

  As-Is LTV              \$14,750,000 / \$18,200,000   **81.04%**

  As-Stabilized LTV      \$14,750,000 / \$23,500,000   **62.77%**

  Loan-to-Cost           \$14,750,000 / \$20,950,000   **70.41%**
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------

The above ratios are provided for the lender's convenience and are calculated based on the proposed loan amount as communicated to the appraiser. The appraiser makes no representation regarding the appropriateness of these ratios for underwriting purposes.

## 8. Assumptions and Limiting Conditions

1.  The appraiser assumes responsible ownership and competent management of the property.

2.  The legal description and title information were obtained from public records and the title commitment issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, effective February 28, 2025). The appraiser assumes title is marketable and insurable.

3.  The appraiser has made no independent survey of the property and relies on the ALTA/NSPS survey dated January 2025 provided by the client.

4.  The appraiser is not an environmental consultant. Environmental information is based on the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment by Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC (Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025). The appraiser assumes the environmental information provided is accurate and complete.

5.  The as-stabilized value is subject to the extraordinary assumption that the \$3,150,000 renovation program will be completed substantially in accordance with the borrower's plans and budget, and that the property will achieve 95% occupancy within the projected timeframe. If this assumption is not realized, the as-stabilized value may differ materially from the opinion stated herein.

6.  The appraiser has inspected the property interior and exterior. Concealed conditions or latent defects not observable during the inspection are not accounted for in this report.

7.  The appraiser assumes compliance with all applicable zoning ordinances, building codes, and land use restrictions, including the SCDHEC land use restriction recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, Charleston County RMC.

8.  Possession of this report does not confer the right of publication or use for any purpose other than the stated intended use.

9.  The appraiser's compensation is not contingent upon the value conclusion, the occurrence of a subsequent event, or the outcome of the loan transaction.

## 9. Certification

I certify that, to the best of my knowledge and belief:

The statements of fact contained in this report are true and correct. The reported analyses, opinions, and conclusions are limited only by the reported assumptions and limiting conditions and are my personal, impartial, and unbiased professional analyses, opinions, and conclusions. I have no present or prospective interest in the property that is the subject of this report and no personal interest with respect to the parties involved. I have no bias with respect to the property that is the subject of this report or to the parties involved with this assignment.

My engagement in this assignment was not contingent upon developing or reporting predetermined results. My compensation for completing this assignment is not contingent upon the development or reporting of a predetermined value or direction in value that favors the cause of the client, the amount of the value opinion, the attainment of a stipulated result, or the occurrence of a subsequent event directly related to the intended use of this appraisal.

My analyses, opinions, and conclusions were developed, and this report has been prepared, in conformity with the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) as promulgated by The Appraisal Foundation.

I have made a personal inspection of the property that is the subject of this report, including both the interior and exterior of the improvements. No one provided significant real property appraisal assistance to the person signing this certification.

I am competent to perform this appraisal assignment by virtue of my education, experience, and professional credentials. I am a South Carolina Certified General Real Estate Appraiser, License No. SC-CGA-04817.

"""Generate a .docx from markdown via Pandoc with an optional reference template.

Usage:
    python generate_from_md.py input.md output.docx [template.docx]

Pandoc applies the template's paragraph and run styles to your markdown.
Best for reports/memos/letters where the template carries firm styling.

Requires pandoc on PATH.
"""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def generate(md_path: Path, output_path: Path, template_path: Path | None = None):
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cmd = ["pandoc", str(md_path), "-o", str(output_path)]
    if template_path is not None:
        cmd.append(f"--reference-doc={template_path}")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"pandoc failed: {result.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        print("Usage: generate_from_md.py <input.md> <output.docx> [template.docx]", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    template = Path(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) == 4 else None
    generate(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), template)

# ARTICLE 2 — THE LOAN, THE NOTE AND PAYMENT TERMS

**2.1 The Note; Principal Amount.** Borrower has executed and delivered the Note in the original principal amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($14,750,000.00), representing the Initial Advance and the Renovation Holdback. The outstanding principal balance of the Note, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and all other Secured Obligations, shall be due and payable on the Maturity Date.

**2.2 Interest Rate.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan at a floating rate per annum equal to Daily SOFR plus two hundred eighty-five (285) basis points (2.85%), provided that, for purposes of determining the applicable rate, Daily SOFR shall not be less than the SOFR Floor. Interest shall be computed on the basis of the actual number of days elapsed over a year of three hundred sixty (360) days.

**2.3 Payments.** Accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be due and payable monthly in arrears on the fifteenth (15th) day of each calendar month (each, a "**Payment Date**"), commencing on May 15, 2025, with the final payment due on the Maturity Date. All payments shall be made in lawful money of the United States, in immediately available funds, to Lender at its address for payment set forth in Section 16.6 or to such other account as Lender may designate in writing, without setoff, deduction, counterclaim or withholding of any kind.

**2.4 Interest-Only Period; Amortization.** From the Closing Date through and including April 15, 2027 (the "**Interest-Only Period**"), each monthly payment shall consist solely of accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan. Commencing with the Payment Date occurring on May 15, 2027, and continuing on each Payment Date thereafter through and including the Maturity Date, each monthly payment shall consist of principal and interest in the amount necessary to fully amortize the then outstanding principal balance of the Loan over a twenty-five (25) year amortization schedule at the interest rate then in effect (after giving effect to the SOFR Floor), with the entire remaining unpaid principal balance, all accrued and unpaid interest and all other Secured Obligations due and payable on the Maturity Date. Borrower acknowledges that the Loan is a balloon loan and that the scheduled monthly payments after the Interest-Only Period will not fully amortize the Loan over its term.

**2.5 Default Rate.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan and, to the extent permitted by applicable law, all other Secured Obligations, shall bear interest at the Default Rate, accruing from the date of the Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or the Loan is repaid in full, whichever first occurs. The application of the Default Rate is not a waiver of any Event of Default nor a waiver of Lender's right to accelerate the Loan, and interest at the Default Rate shall be a Secured Obligation.

**2.6 Late Charge.** If any monthly installment of principal and/or interest is not received by Lender within ten (10) calendar days after the applicable Payment Date, Borrower shall pay to Lender, on demand, a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue installment. Borrower acknowledges that the late charge is intended to compensate Lender for the additional administrative expense of processing late payments and is not a penalty, and that the late charge is payable whether or not an Event of Default has occurred and whether or not Lender has given notice. The late charge is in addition to, and not in lieu of, interest at the Default Rate.

**2.7 Maximum Lawful Rate; Savings Clause.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Mortgage or the other Loan Documents, in no event shall the total interest and other charges contracted for, charged or received by Lender under the Loan Documents exceed the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. If any amount in excess of such maximum is charged or received, (a) it shall be deemed a mistake and shall be cancelled automatically, or, at Lender's option, applied to reduce the principal balance of the Loan, and (b) the effective rate of interest shall be automatically reduced to the maximum lawful rate, and any amounts previously paid in excess of such rate shall be credited against the principal balance of the Loan. To the extent permitted by applicable law, all amounts that constitute interest shall be amortized, prorated, allocated and spread over the full period of the Loan.

**2.8 Application and Order of Payments.** All payments received by Lender shall be applied (a) first, to any sums advanced by Lender for the protection of the Collateral, (b) second, to late charges, prepayment premiums and other fees then due, (c) third, to accrued and unpaid interest, (d) fourth, to principal, and (e) fifth, to any other Secured Obligations, in each case in such order as Lender may determine in its discretion and in accordance with the Note. # ARTICLE 2 — THE LOAN, THE NOTE AND PAYMENT TERMS

**2.1 The Note; Principal Amount.** Borrower has executed and delivered the Note in the original principal amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($14,750,000.00), representing the Initial Advance and the Renovation Holdback. The outstanding principal balance of the Note, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and all other Secured Obligations, shall be due and payable on the Maturity Date.

**2.2 Interest Rate.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan at a floating rate per annum equal to Daily SOFR plus two hundred eighty-five (285) basis points (2.85%), provided that, for purposes of determining the applicable rate, Daily SOFR shall not be less than the SOFR Floor. Interest shall be computed on the basis of the actual number of days elapsed over a year of three hundred sixty (360) days.

**2.3 Payments.** Accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be due and payable monthly in arrears on the fifteenth (15th) day of each calendar month (each, a "**Payment Date**"), commencing on May 15, 2025, with the final payment due on the Maturity Date. All payments shall be made in lawful money of the United States, in immediately available funds, to Lender at its address for payment set forth in Section 16.6 or to such other account as Lender may designate in writing, without setoff, deduction, counterclaim or withholding of any kind.

**2.4 Interest-Only Period; Amortization.** From the Closing Date through and including April 15, 2027 (the "**Interest-Only Period**"), each monthly payment shall consist solely of accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan. Commencing with the Payment Date occurring on May 15, 2027, and continuing on each Payment Date thereafter through and including the Maturity Date, each monthly payment shall consist of principal and interest in the amount necessary to fully amortize the then outstanding principal balance of the Loan over a twenty-five (25) year amortization schedule at the interest rate then in effect (after giving effect to the SOFR Floor), with the entire remaining unpaid principal balance, all accrued and unpaid interest and all other Secured Obligations due and payable on the Maturity Date. Borrower acknowledges that the Loan is a balloon loan and that the scheduled monthly payments after the Interest-Only Period will not fully amortize the Loan over its term.

**2.5 Default Rate.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the outstanding principal balance of the Loan and, to the extent permitted by applicable law, all other Secured Obligations, shall bear interest at the Default Rate, accruing from the date of the Event of Default until such Event of Default is cured or the Loan is repaid in full, whichever first occurs. The application of the Default Rate is not a waiver of any Event of Default nor a waiver of Lender's right to accelerate the Loan, and interest at the Default Rate shall be a Secured Obligation.

**2.6 Late Charge.** If any monthly installment of principal and/or interest is not received by Lender within ten (10) calendar days after the applicable Payment Date, Borrower shall pay to Lender, on demand, a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue installment. Borrower acknowledges that the late charge is intended to compensate Lender for the additional administrative expense of processing late payments and is not a penalty, and that the late charge is payable whether or not an Event of Default has occurred and whether or not Lender has given notice. The late charge is in addition to, and not in lieu of, interest at the Default Rate.

**2.7 Maximum Lawful Rate; Savings Clause.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Mortgage or the other Loan Documents, in no event shall the total interest and other charges contracted for, charged or received by Lender under the Loan Documents exceed the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. If any amount in excess of such maximum is charged or received, (a) it shall be deemed a mistake and shall be cancelled automatically, or, at Lender's option, applied to reduce the principal balance of the Loan, and (b) the effective rate of interest shall be automatically reduced to the maximum lawful rate, and any amounts previously paid in excess of such rate shall be credited against the principal balance of the Loan. To the extent permitted by applicable law, all amounts that constitute interest shall be amortized, prorated, allocated and spread over the full period of the Loan.

**2.8 Application and Order of Payments.** All payments received by Lender shall be applied (a) first, to any sums advanced by Lender for the protection of the Collateral, (b) second, to late charges, prepayment premiums and other fees then due, (c) third, to accrued and unpaid interest, (d) fourth, to principal, and (e) fifth, to any other Secured Obligations, in each case in such order as Lender may determine in its discretion and in accordance with the Note. Any payment received after 2:00 p.m. Eastern time on a Business Day shall be deemed received on the next Business Day.

The license granted in this Section 4.2 shall not constitute a waiver of Lender's rights under Section 4.1 or under the Assignment of Rents Act, and shall not be construed as a release or reconveyance of the assignment of Rents.

(a) notify any or all tenants under the Leases, in writing, to pay all Rents directly to Lender or to a depository account designated by Lender, and each such tenant shall thereafter be obligated to make all payments directly to Lender or its designee, and shall be entitled to rely on such notice without inquiry and without liability to Borrower;

(b) collect, sue for, compromise, settle and give receipts for all Rents;

(c) enforce, at Borrower's expense, all terms of the Leases, including the obligation to pay Rents, and exercise all rights and remedies of the landlord thereunder, including the right to evict, terminate, renew, modify, accept surrender of, or otherwise deal with any Lease, without releasing any tenant or guarantor from liability;

(d) apply all Rents received to the Secured Obligations in such order as Lender may determine in accordance with Section 2.8, or, at Lender's election, hold the same as cash collateral for the Secured Obligations; and

(e) take any other action permitted under the Assignment of Rents Act or other applicable law.

**4.4 Tenant Direction Letters; Estoppel Certificates; SNDAs.** Concurrently with the execution of this Mortgage, Borrower shall execute and deliver to Lender, for delivery at Lender's election upon an Event of Default, tenant direction letters in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender, addressed to each tenant under the Leases, directing payment of Rents to Lender. Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and deliver to Lender (a) a tenant estoppel certificate from each tenant in occupancy at the Property, in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender, and (b) a subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreement ("**SNDA**") from each such tenant, in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender. Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, at the first renewal, extension or amendment of such Lease, an amendment adding customary assignment and estoppel provisions.

**4.5 Subordination of Leases; Attornment.** Each Lease now or hereafter existing is and shall be subject and subordinate in all respects to this Mortgage and to all advances made or to be made under the Note, to the full extent of all Rents and other sums secured hereby, unless Lender expressly agrees otherwise in a written SNDA or subordination agreement. Borrower shall not subordinate any Lease to any other mortgage, deed of trust or lien. Borrower shall, upon Lender's request following a foreclosure or conveyance in lieu of foreclosure, cause each tenant under a Lease to attorn to the purchaser or transferee at such foreclosure or conveyance and to recognize such purchaser or transferee as the landlord under its Lease for the balance of the term thereof; and Lender may, in its discretion, deliver a commercially reasonable non-disturbance agreement to any tenant. Any SNDA delivered by Lender may provide that the tenant's rights of first refusal, rights of first offer, options to purchase and other purchase rights (including the right of first refusal held by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to Bay 2) shall not be binding upon, or enforceable against, Lender or any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee in lieu of foreclosure.

**4.6 Security Deposits.** Borrower's interest in all security deposits and other tenant deposits now or hereafter held under the Leases is hereby assigned to Lender as part of the Collateral; provided, however, that Lender shall have no liability or responsibility with respect to any security deposit unless and until actually received by Lender, and Lender shall have no obligation to hold security deposits in a segregated account or to pay interest thereon except as required by applicable law or the applicable Lease. Borrower shall hold all security deposits in accordance with applicable law and the applicable Leases, and shall not apply any security deposit except as permitted by the applicable Lease and applicable law.

**4.7 No Liability of Lender; Authority.** Lender shall not be obligated to perform any obligation of Borrower under any Lease, to appear in or defend any action relating to any Lease, or to incur any expense in connection therewith, unless Lender elects in writing to do so. Borrower hereby irrevocably appoints Lender as its attorney-in-fact, effective upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, to execute and deliver in Borrower's name, place and stead all notices, instruments and agreements reasonably necessary to enforce the assignment of Rents and the Leases, which appointment is coupled with an interest and is irrevocable. The exercise of the rights granted in this Article 4 shall not make Lender a mortgagee in possession, shall not constitute an assumption by Lender of any obligation under any Lease, and shall not impair Lender's right to pursue any other remedy.

**4.8 No Release of Borrower.** Nothing in this Article 4 shall release Borrower from any liability or obligation under any Lease or the Loan Documents, and Borrower shall remain liable for the performance of all landlord obligations under the Leases and for the payment of the Secured Obligations.

**7.3 Transfer Restrictions.**

(a) Sell, convey, transfer, assign, mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, encumber or otherwise dispose of the Property or any portion thereof or interest therein, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, including any easement, leasehold interest, license, right-of-way grant, dedication, subdivision, condominium conversion or air rights transfer, except Leases entered into in compliance with Section 6.7.

(c) Permit any change in the Control of Borrower, Graydon Development Group LLC, Guarantor, or any other Person that Controls Borrower, whether by transfer of direct or indirect ownership interests, merger, consolidation, conversion, reorganization, sale of all or substantially all of the assets of any such Person, or the replacement, resignation or removal of the Independent Manager, whether or not such transaction constitutes a transfer of a membership interest in Borrower under the Operating Agreement. Borrower acknowledges that the Operating Agreement does not currently restrict indirect or upstream changes in the ownership, control or management of Borrower's Members and that this Section 7.3(c) is intended to capture such changes.

# ARTICLE 4 — ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT OF LEASES AND RENTS

This assignment is made pursuant to and is intended to be effective under the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act, as enacted in Title 29, Chapter 3 of the South Carolina Code of Laws. **4.3 Enforcement Upon Default.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Lender may, in its sole discretion and without the necessity of obtaining a court order, appointing a receiver, entering into possession, or taking any other action, and without regard to the adequacy of the value of the Collateral:

(a) notify any or all tenants under the Leases, in writing, to pay all Rents directly to Lender or to a depository account designated by Lender, and each such tenant shall thereafter be obligated to make all payments directly to Lender or its designee, and shall be entitled to rely on such notice without inquiry and without liability to Borrower;

(d) apply all Rents received to the Secured Obligations in such order as Lender may determine in accordance with Section 2.8, or, at Lender's election, hold the same as cash collateral for the Secured Obligations; and

(a) engage in no business or activity other than the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, management and disposition of the Property and activities incidental thereto;

(b) maintain its own separate books of account, financial records and bank accounts, separate and apart from those of any other Person;

(c) not commingle its funds or assets with those of any Affiliate, Member, manager or other Person;

(d) hold itself out to the public as a legal entity separate and distinct from any other Person, including its Members and Affiliates, and conduct its business in its own name, using its own stationery, invoices, checks and accounts;

(e) maintain adequate capitalization in light of its contemplated business operations, transactions and liabilities;

(f) pay its own liabilities from its own assets and not pay or guaranty the liabilities of any Affiliate;

(g) observe all limited liability company formalities and maintain an arms'-length relationship with its Affiliates;

(h) not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any other Person;

(i) not acquire obligations or securities of its Members or Affiliates, and not pledge its assets for the benefit of any other Person except as contemplated by the Loan Documents;

(j) not incur any additional indebtedness, whether secured or unsecured, without Lender's prior written consent, in accordance with Section 7.1;

(k) not dissolve, liquidate, merge, consolidate or wind up its affairs, and not file or consent to any petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code or any other insolvency proceeding, without the affirmative vote of the Independent Manager and Lender's prior written consent; and

(l) not amend, modify or waive any single-purpose entity provision of its organizational documents without Lender's prior written consent in each instance.

**6.13 Management of the Property.** Manage the Property in a commercially reasonable manner consistent with the standards described in Section 6.4, and not enter into, or permit any amendment to or termination of, any management agreement, leasing agreement or similar agreement affecting the Property without Lender's prior written consent. [Borrower's management of the Property is subject to Lender's right to require a management agreement in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender.]

**6.14 Contracts, Warranties and Claims.** Perform all of Borrower's obligations under the GC Contract, architect's agreements, maintenance contracts, equipment warranties and other contracts relating to the Property; enforce all warranties, guaranties and indemnities for the benefit of Lender; and not terminate, amend or waive any material right thereunder without Lender's prior written consent.

**6.15 Defense of the Collateral; Lender's Right to Cure.** Defend the Collateral against all claims and demands of all Persons, and appear in and defend any action or proceeding that may affect the Collateral, Lender's interest therein or the lien or priority of this Mortgage. If Borrower fails to perform any covenant or fails to pay any Imposition, insurance premium, mechanic's claim or other charge affecting the Collateral, or fails to comply with the LUR or any Environmental Law, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to), after five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to Borrower (or immediately if Lender reasonably determines that an emergency exists or that the Collateral or Lender's interest therein is at risk), pay, perform or cure the same, and all amounts so expended, together with interest at the Default Rate from the date of expenditure and all costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), shall be Secured Obligations payable on demand and secured by this Mortgage.

**6.16 Notices.** Promptly, and in any event within five (5) Business Days, notify Lender in writing of (a) any Event of Default or any event that with notice or lapse of time, or both, would constitute an Event of Default; (b) any litigation, arbitration, governmental proceeding, citation, violation or order affecting Borrower, Guarantor or the Property that involves a claim in excess of $100,000 or that could materially and adversely affect the Property or the Collateral; (c) any fire or other casualty, condemnation or threatened condemnation affecting the Property; (d) any actual or threatened release of Hazardous Materials at the Property, any violation of the LUR, any inspection, investigation, notice of violation, order or correspondence from SCDHEC or any other environmental authority relating to the Property, and any breach, modification or termination of the LUR; (e) any material change in the ownership or management of Borrower or Guarantor; and (f) any default under the GC Contract or cessation of the Renovation for more than ten (10) consecutive days.

**6.17 Completion of the Renovation.** Complete the Renovation in accordance with the Plans, the Renovation Budget and Article 8, on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline, and obtain a certificate of occupancy (or equivalent) from the City of Charleston for the renovated portions of the Property.

**6.18 Maintenance of Perfection.** Take all action necessary to maintain the perfection, priority and enforceability of Lender's lien on and security interest in the Collateral and Lender's interest in the Leases and Rents, including the filing of continuation statements and the recording of any supplemental instruments.

**6.19 Lender's Expenses.** Reimburse Lender, on demand, for all reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by Lender in connection with the administration, monitoring, enforcement and protection of the Loan and the Collateral, including legal fees, construction inspection fees, appraisal and environmental review fees, and the cost of any protective advance, together with interest at the Default Rate if not reimbursed within ten (10) days after demand, all of which shall be Secured Obligations.

# ARTICLE 7 — NEGATIVE COVENANTS; SINGLE-PURPOSE ENTITY

From and after the Closing Date and until the Secured Obligations are paid and performed in full, Borrower shall not, without Lender's prior written consent:

**7.1 Indebtedness.** Incur, create, assume, guarantee or permit to exist any indebtedness, whether secured or unsecured, direct or contingent, including any mezzanine loan, preferred equity investment or other financing arrangement, other than the Secured Obligations and trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business and not more than ninety (90) days past due.

**7.2 Liens.** Create, incur, assume or permit to exist any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, pledge, security interest, charge, encumbrance, judgment lien, mechanics' or materialmen's lien, tax lien, or other lien or encumbrance on the Property or any other Collateral, or any portion thereof or interest therein, whether senior, pari passu or subordinate to this Mortgage, other than the lien of this Mortgage and the Permitted Exceptions.

**7.3 Transfer Restrictions.**

(a) Sell, convey, transfer, assign, mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, encumber or otherwise dispose of the Property or any portion thereof or interest therein, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, including any easement, leasehold interest, license, right-of-way grant, dedication, subdivision, condominium conversion or air rights transfer, except Leases entered into in compliance with Section 6.7.

(b) Permit any transfer, sale, assignment, pledge, hypothecation or other disposition of any ownership or economic interest in Borrower or any interest therein exceeding ten percent (10%) individually or twenty-five percent (25%) in the aggregate, other than transfers among the existing Members of Borrower (Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC) that are permitted under and consummated in accordance with the Operating Agreement and as to which Borrower has given Lender at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice and such transferee has confirmed in writing that it is bound by the single-purpose entity provisions of Section 6.12.

(c) Permit any change in the Control of Borrower, Graydon Development Group LLC, Guarantor, or any other Person that Controls Borrower, whether by transfer of direct or indirect ownership interests, merger, consolidation, conversion, reorganization, sale of all or substantially all of the assets of any such Person, or the replacement, resignation or removal of the Independent Manager, whether or not such transaction constitutes a transfer of a membership interest in Borrower under the Operating Agreement. Borrower acknowledges that the Operating Agreement does not currently restrict indirect or upstream changes in the ownership, control or management of Borrower's Members and that this Section 7.3(c) is intended to capture such changes.

(d) Permit any transfer of any interest in the Property or in Borrower while an Event of Default exists, or in connection with any transaction intended to avoid the restrictions of this Section 7.3.

Any transfer in violation of this Section 7.3 shall be void ab initio at Lender's election, shall constitute an immediate Event of Default without notice or opportunity to cure in accordance with Section 14.1(g), and shall entitle Lender to exercise all remedies available under Article 14 and under applicable law.

**7.4 Change in Use; Prohibition on Residential Conversion.** Change the use of the Property, or any portion thereof, from mixed-use retail and office use consistent with the GB (General Business) zoning classification, or use or permit the use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007, comprising Bay 1 at 520 King Street) for any residential purpose, dwelling, overnight occupancy or purpose that would violate the LUR, or take any action that would constitute a modification, termination or violation of the LUR.

**7.5 Alterations and Demolition.** Demolish, raze, materially alter, remove or add to any improvement on the Property, or remove any fixture, building system, equipment or personal property forming part of the Collateral (except replacement with property of substantially equal or better quality), except for (a) the Renovation in accordance with Article 8, (b) tenant improvements required under Leases approved by Lender or entered into in compliance with Section 6.7, and (c) ordinary repair and maintenance in accordance with Section 6.4.

**7.6 Amendments to Organizational Documents; Single-Purpose Entity Provisions.**

(a) Amend, modify, restate, waive, repeal or suspend any provision of Borrower's organizational documents, including the Operating Agreement, without Lender's prior written consent in each instance; provided that Borrower may, without Lender's consent, make amendments that do not adversely affect Lender or the Collateral and that do not affect any single-purpose entity, separateness, independent manager, bankruptcy-remote or transfer restriction provision.

(b) Operate or permit its organizational documents to be operated in a manner inconsistent with any single-purpose entity provision. "**Operating Agreement Amendment**" means the amendment to the Operating Agreement, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Lender, executed by all three Members of Borrower (including Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, acting through its general partner Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC), effective not later than the Closing Date, which adds and implements (i) the requirement of an Independent Manager whose affirmative vote is required before Borrower may institute or consent to any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding, dissolve, liquidate, merge, consolidate or wind up its affairs, (ii) the separateness covenants described in Section 6.12, (iii) a single-purpose purpose clause restricting Borrower's business to the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, management and financing of the Property and activities incidental thereto, (iv) a requirement that any amendment or modification of the foregoing provisions require unanimity of the Members and Lender's written consent, and (v) such other provisions as Lender may reasonably require to confirm that the restrictions in this Mortgage are binding on all Members. Borrower acknowledges that, as of the date of the Term Sheet, the Operating Agreement did not contain such provisions, and Borrower shall not make any representation inconsistent with this acknowledgment.

(c) Cause or permit Borrower to (i) have any assets other than those related to the Property, (ii) have any indebtedness other than as permitted by Section 7.1, (iii) be named as a direct or contingent beneficiary or loss payee on any insurance policy of any Affiliate, or (iv) identify Borrower as a division or part of any other Person.

**7.7 Amendments and Terminations of Leases.** Amend, modify, extend, renew, terminate, accept the surrender of, or waive any material right under any Lease, or consent to any assignment or sublease under any Lease, except that Borrower may, without Lender's consent, (a) take any such action with respect to a Lease if the action is required by the terms of the Lease or by applicable law, and (b) take any such action that does not reduce rent, shorten the term, increase landlord obligations or decrease tenant obligations, in each case subject to the restrictions in Section 6.7. Lender's prior written consent shall be required for (i) any new Lease or amendment for premises in excess of five thousand (5,000) square feet, (ii) any new Lease or renewal for a term in excess of five (5) years (including any renewal or extension options), (iii) any Lease containing a right of first refusal, right of first offer, option to purchase, exclusivity, co-tenancy, termination or kick-out right, and (iv) any termination, surrender or cancellation of a Lease prior to its stated expiration. Lender's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Borrower shall deliver to Lender copies of all executed leases and lease amendments within ten (10) business days after execution, in accordance with Section 12.3(e).

**7.8 Easements, Dedications, Subdivision and Restrictions.** Grant any easement, license, right-of-way or encroachment agreement, dedicate any portion of the Property to any public or private use, subdivide the Property, record any declaration, covenant, condition or restriction affecting the Property, impose any restrictive covenant, or enter into any agreement with any adjoining owner, without Lender's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld with respect to grants that do not materially impair the value, use, access or marketability of the Property; provided that Borrower shall not permit any action described in this Section 7.8 that could reasonably be expected to impair the priority of this Mortgage or the Collateral. Any such instrument to which Lender consents shall recite that it is subject and subordinate to this Mortgage.

**7.9 Hazardous Materials.** Cause or permit any Hazardous Materials to be brought upon, treated, kept, stored, disposed of, released or transported to, from or at the Property, or any activity that would violate any Environmental Law or the LUR, except for de minimis quantities of customary office, cleaning, maintenance and (in the case of the specialty grocery tenant) food-service supplies that are used, stored and disposed of in compliance with applicable Environmental Laws and the Leases; provided that no activity shall be permitted that would reasonably be expected to result in the reopening of SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772, the impairment of the No Further Action status of the Property, or the imposition of any institutional control in addition to the LUR.

**7.10 Affiliate Transactions.** Enter into any transaction or agreement with any Affiliate of Borrower, Guarantor or any Member of Borrower, including any management, leasing, development or asset management agreement, except on arms'-length terms, disclosed in writing to Lender, and approved in writing by Lender.

**7.11 Distributions; Payments to Members.** Make any distribution, dividend, return of capital, loan repayment or other payment to any Member or Affiliate, or redeem or repurchase any membership interest, (a) during the continuance of an Event of Default, or (b) if, after giving effect to such payment, Borrower would fail to maintain the net worth or liquidity required by Section 12.2.

# ARTICLE 8 — RENOVATION AND CONSTRUCTION

**8.1 The Renovation Holdback.** Lender shall hold the Renovation Holdback and shall disburse the same to Borrower from time to time in accordance with this Article 8 for the purpose of paying Renovation Costs (as defined in Section 8.2). Lender shall have no obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback unless and until each applicable condition in Section 8.5 has been satisfied. The Renovation Holdback is a portion of the Loan and bears interest from the Closing Date regardless of whether it has been disbursed, in accordance with the Note.

**8.2 Renovation Budget; Renovation Costs; Reallocations.** "**Renovation Costs**" means all hard and soft costs of completing the Renovation in accordance with the Plans, the GC Contract and the Renovation Budget, including the cost of construction, labor, materials, tenant improvement allowances, architects', engineers' and consultants' fees, permit and inspection fees, construction management fees, builder's risk and other insurance attributable to the Renovation, and the contingency set forth in the Renovation Budget. Borrower shall cause the Renovation to be completed in accordance with the Renovation Budget attached as **Exhibit D**. Borrower may reallocate amounts among line items of the Renovation Budget without Lender's consent, provided that (a) no reallocation increases the total Renovation Budget, (b) no reallocation increases the amount allocated to any line item by more than ten percent (10%) of such line item, (c) no reallocation decreases the contingent or soft-cost line items below the amounts shown on **Exhibit D**, and (d) Borrower delivers to Lender written notice of the reallocation within ten (10) business days. Any reallocation not satisfying the foregoing shall require Lender's prior written consent.

**8.3 Borrower Equity; Cost Overruns.** Borrower shall fund, from its own funds and not from Loan proceeds, the portion of the Renovation Costs not funded by the Renovation Holdback, being not less than Nine Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($900,000) (the "**Renovation Equity**"), together with all costs of the Renovation in excess of the Renovation Budget and all costs of completing the Renovation not funded by the Renovation Holdback. Borrower shall not be entitled to any reimbursement of the Renovation Equity from Loan proceeds. If at any time Lender reasonably determines that the undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback is insufficient to pay the remaining Renovation Costs, Borrower shall, within fifteen (15) days after Lender's written demand, deposit with Lender an amount equal to the deficiency, which amount shall be disbursed by Lender in accordance with this Article 8. Borrower shall fund its share of Renovation Costs such that at no time shall the aggregate amount disbursed from the Renovation Holdback exceed seventy-one and four hundred thirty-eight thousandths percent (71.438%) of the aggregate Renovation Costs incurred and certified to Lender as of such date (being the ratio of the Renovation Holdback, $2,250,000, to the Renovation Budget, $3,150,000).

**8.4 Draw Request Procedure.**

(a) Borrower may request a disbursement from the Renovation Holdback no more frequently than once per calendar month, by delivering to Lender a written draw request not less than ten (10) Business Days prior to the requested disbursement date.

(b) Each draw request shall be substantially in the form attached as **Exhibit E**, shall be signed by Borrower and certified by Borrower's architect of record, and shall include: (i) an AIA G702/G703 Application and Certificate for Payment detailing the work completed, the amounts previously paid, the amount currently requested and the percentage of completion; (ii) a schedule of the line items of the Renovation Budget to which the requested disbursement is to be applied and the remaining balance of each such line item; (iii) conditional lien waivers for the current draw and unconditional lien waivers for all prior draws from the General Contractor and each subcontractor performing work in an amount exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($25,000.00); (iv) a title date-down endorsement from the title insurer confirming that no intervening mechanics', materialmen's or other liens or encumbrances have been recorded against the Property since the date of this Mortgage or the most recent date-down endorsement, as applicable; (v) evidence of Lender's satisfactory inspection of the work in progress in accordance with Section 8.9; (vi) invoices or other evidence of the costs for which reimbursement is requested, to the extent reasonably requested by Lender; (vii) a certification that Borrower has funded its portion of Renovation Costs in accordance with Section 8.3; and (viii) such other information as Lender may reasonably request.

(c) Lender shall, within ten (10) Business Days after receipt of a complete and conforming draw request and satisfaction of the conditions in Section 8.5, disburse the requested amount, less the retainage required by Section 8.6, directly to Borrower or, at Lender's election, to the General Contractor, subcontractors, materialmen or other Persons entitled to payment, by joint check or otherwise.

**8.5 Conditions to Each Disbursement.** Lender's obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback is subject to satisfaction of each of the following conditions, each in form and substance satisfactory to Lender:

(a) no Event of Default or event that with notice or lapse of time, or both, would constitute an Event of Default shall have occurred and be continuing;

(b) all representations and warranties in Article 5 shall be true and correct in all material respects;

(c) the Renovation shall be proceeding in accordance with the Plans and the Renovation Budget, and there shall exist no material defect, deficiency or departure from the Plans;

(d) each condition set forth in Section 8.4 shall have been satisfied and all documents required thereunder shall have been delivered to Lender;

(e) Borrower shall have funded the Renovation Equity in accordance with Section 8.3;

(f) no mechanics' or materialmen's lien shall have been filed against the Property and remain undischarged or unbonded, and the title insurer shall have issued the date-down endorsement required by Section 8.4(b)(iv);

(g) all building permits, Board of Architectural Review approvals (to the extent required for the work in question) and other governmental approvals required for the work shall have been obtained;

(h) if the work in question involves any penetration of, alteration to, or work within ten (10) feet of the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, Borrower shall have delivered to Lender (i) evidence of written notice to SCDHEC as required by the LUR, (ii) a vapor barrier protection and restoration plan prepared by a licensed environmental professional reasonably acceptable to Lender, and (iii) a certification from such professional that the vapor barrier has been inspected and, following the work, restored in accordance with the LUR; and

(i) Lender shall have received evidence that the undisbursed Renovation Holdback, together with Borrower's remaining unfunded Renovation Equity commitment, is sufficient to complete the Renovation in accordance with the Renovation Budget.

**8.6 Retainage.** Lender shall retain ten percent (10%) of each disbursement from the Renovation Holdback (the "**Retainage**") until Substantial Completion has been achieved in accordance with Section 8.11. Retainage shall be released in accordance with Section 8.15.

**8.7 Plans and Specifications; Permits; Board of Architectural Review.** The Renovation shall be performed in accordance with the Plans approved by Lender. Borrower shall not amend, modify or supplement the Plans in any manner that constitutes a Major Change (as defined in Section 8.8) without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall obtain and maintain in full force and effect all permits, licenses and approvals necessary for the Renovation, including any approval of the City of Charleston Board of Architectural Review applicable to the façade restoration and to the decorative iron balcony described in Section 5.14, and shall deliver copies thereof to Lender upon request.

**8.8 GC Contract; Change Orders.** Borrower has delivered to Lender a complete copy of the GC Contract, including all schedules, exhibits and amendments. Borrower shall not amend, modify, supplement, terminate or accept the assignment of the GC Contract, and shall not approve or enter into any change order, amendment or supplemental agreement under the GC Contract, without Lender's prior written consent if such action (a) increases the contract sum of the GC Contract or the Renovation Budget, (b) reduces the scope of the Renovation, (c) affects the structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, elevator or façade systems, (d) affects the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7 or the vapor barrier beneath such slab, or (e) would reasonably be expected to delay Substantial Completion beyond the Substantial Completion Deadline (each, a "**Major Change**"). Borrower hereby assigns to Lender, as part of the Collateral, all of Borrower's right, title and interest in, to and under the GC Contract and the Plans, and shall cause the General Contractor and Borrower's architect to execute and deliver to Lender a consent to such assignment and collateral assignment in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender.

**8.9 Inspections.** Lender, and any third-party inspector retained by Lender (at Borrower's expense), may inspect the Property and the work in progress at any reasonable time upon reasonable prior notice, and Borrower shall provide access and such information as Lender or its inspector may request. Borrower shall cause the work to be corrected promptly if any inspection discloses defective work or a departure from the Plans. Borrower acknowledges that no inspection by Lender shall constitute a waiver of any default, an approval of any work, or an assumption of responsibility for the adequacy, legality or quality of the Renovation, and that Lender has no duty to inspect.

**8.10 Mechanic's Liens; Lien Waivers; Title Date-Downs.** Borrower shall pay when due all costs of the Renovation and shall keep the Property free from mechanics', materialmen's and other liens. If any such lien is filed, Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days after notice thereof, cause the lien to be discharged of record or bonded over in a manner reasonably satisfactory to Lender and the title insurer. Borrower shall obtain unconditional lien waivers from the General Contractor and all subcontractors as a condition to each disbursement, and shall obtain a final title date-down endorsement and final lien waivers as a condition to the release of Retainage. Borrower shall not permit any stop notice, notice of nonpayment or similar claim to remain undischarged in a manner that could impair the Property or Lender's lien.

**8.11 Substantial Completion; Substantial Completion Deadline.** Borrower shall achieve Substantial Completion of the Renovation on or before June 15, 2026, time being of the essence. Borrower shall notify Lender in writing not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the anticipated date of Substantial Completion, and shall deliver to Lender (a) a certificate of Substantial Completion from Borrower's architect, (b) a copy of the certificate of occupancy (or equivalent) issued by the City of Charleston for the renovated portions of the Property, (c) a certification that the Renovation has been completed in accordance with the Plans and within the Renovation Budget, and (d) evidence that all costs of the Renovation have been paid or will be paid from the final disbursement. Failure to achieve Substantial Completion on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline shall constitute an Event of Default in accordance with Section 14.1(h) and shall entitle Lender to exercise its rights under the Completion Guaranty.

**8.12 Failure to Complete; Deemed Completion.** If Borrower fails to achieve Substantial Completion by the Substantial Completion Deadline, then, in addition to Lender's other remedies, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to) assume responsibility for completing the Renovation, and all amounts expended by Lender in doing so, together with interest at the Default Rate, shall be Secured Obligations. Lender's exercise of any right under this Section 8.12 shall not release Borrower or Guarantor from any obligation under the Loan Documents or the Completion Guaranty.

**8.13 Coordination with the LUR and Vapor Barrier.** Borrower shall cause the General Contractor, all subcontractors, Borrower's architect and all other Persons performing work at the Property to be informed in writing of the existence and location of the vapor barrier beneath the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, of the restrictions imposed by the LUR, and of the requirements of Section 11.3, prior to the commencement of any work at the Property. Borrower shall not permit any penetration, removal, alteration or compromise of the vapor barrier, and shall not permit any work affecting the Bay 1 slab, without (a) prior written notice to SCDHEC in accordance with the LUR, (b) Lender's prior written consent, and (c) supervision and post-work inspection and certification by a licensed environmental professional reasonably acceptable to Lender, all at Borrower's expense.

**8.14 No Obligation to Complete; No Lender Liability.** Lender shall have no obligation to complete the Renovation, to advance any amount in excess of the Renovation Holdback, or to pay any cost of the Renovation in excess of the amounts available in the Renovation Holdback and Borrower's Renovation Equity. Lender's approval of the Plans, the Renovation Budget, the GC Contract or any draw request, and any inspection by Lender or its consultant, shall not constitute a representation or warranty by Lender as to the adequacy, sufficiency, quality, legality or feasibility of the Renovation or the Plans, and Lender shall have no liability to Borrower or any other Person with respect thereto. Borrower acknowledges that Borrower, and not Lender, is the owner of the Property and the party responsible for the Renovation.

**8.15 Retainage Release; Final Disbursement.** Upon Lender's receipt of satisfactory evidence of Substantial Completion, final unconditional lien waivers from the General Contractor and all subcontractors and materialmen, a final title date-down endorsement, the certificate of occupancy, and confirmation that the vapor barrier and all LUR requirements have been satisfied, Lender shall release the Retainage and make the final disbursement from the Renovation Holdback. Lender may withhold the Retainage or any portion thereof until completion of all punch list items reasonably acceptable to Lender.

**8.16 Completion Guaranty.** The obligations of Borrower under this Article 8 are guaranteed by Guarantor pursuant to the Completion Guaranty, which guarantees completion of the Renovation within the Renovation Budget and on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline. Borrower's failure to achieve Substantial Completion by the Substantial Completion Deadline shall constitute a failure under the Completion Guaranty and an Event of Default under this Mortgage.

**8.17 No Waiver.** Acceptance by Borrower of any disbursement, or Lender's approval of any draw request, inspection report or plan, shall not constitute a waiver of any condition, covenant or Event of Default, or an approval of any work not conforming to the Plans.

# ARTICLE 9 — INSURANCE

**9.1 Property Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain at all times during the term of the Loan, at its sole expense, comprehensive all-risk (special form) property insurance covering the Property and all improvements, fixtures and betterments thereon, on a replacement cost basis without deduction for depreciation, with an agreed amount endorsement (waiver of coinsurance) and, if the Property is in a special flood hazard area, flood coverage as required by Section 9.3. Such insurance shall include coverage for fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, explosion, riot and civil commotion, vandalism, malicious mischief, sprinkler leakage, water damage, and such other perils as Lender may reasonably require, and shall include ordinance or law coverage, debris removal, and business income/rental value coverage in an amount not less than twelve (12) months of gross rents and operating expenses.

**9.2 Commercial General Liability.** Borrower shall maintain commercial general liability insurance written on an occurrence basis, with minimum limits of Two Million and No/100 Dollars ($2,000,000.00) per occurrence and Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00) in the aggregate, including coverage for premises liability, operations liability, products and completed operations, personal and advertising injury, and contractual liability (including the liability assumed under this Mortgage), naming Lender as an additional insured. Borrower shall also maintain automobile liability and employers' liability insurance in amounts reasonably satisfactory to Lender.

**9.3 Flood Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain flood insurance with respect to the improvements on the Property in an amount not less than Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00), naming Lender as mortgagee and loss payee. Borrower acknowledges that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard), that flood insurance is not required by federal regulation for properties in Zone X, and that Lender nevertheless requires such flood insurance as a condition of the Loan. Borrower shall deliver to Lender evidence of the flood zone determination and shall comply with all applicable requirements of the Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973, as amended, and the regulations thereunder.

**9.4 Builder's Risk Insurance.** During the period from the Closing Date through Substantial Completion, Borrower shall maintain builder's risk insurance written on a completed value, all-risk basis in an amount not less than Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($3,150,000.00), covering the Property and the Renovation against all risks of physical loss or damage during the course of construction, including coverage for materials in transit and stored off-site, and naming Lender as mortgagee and loss payee. Such coverage may be provided as part of the General Contractor's policy, provided that Lender's interests are protected by an appropriate endorsement and Lender approves the form.

**9.5 Other Insurance.** Borrower shall maintain (a) workers' compensation insurance in the amounts required by the laws of the State of South Carolina, covering all of Borrower's employees and, to the extent not covered by the General Contractor's or a subcontractor's policy, all persons engaged in the Renovation; (b) umbrella/excess liability insurance with limits of not less than Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00) per occurrence and in the aggregate, providing excess coverage over commercial general liability, automobile liability and employers' liability; and (c) such other insurance, in such amounts and covering such risks, as Lender may reasonably require from time to time.

**9.6 Carrier Ratings; Policy Terms.** All insurance required under this Article 9 shall be issued by insurers licensed or authorized to do business in the State of South Carolina, having an A.M. Best rating of not less than A-:VII, and shall be written on forms reasonably acceptable to Lender. # ARTICLE 10 — RESERVES AND ESCROWS

**10.1 Tax and Insurance Escrow.** Borrower shall make monthly deposits with Lender, on each Payment Date, in an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual Impositions and casualty and liability insurance premiums for the Property (for all three tax parcels described on **Exhibit A**), as reasonably determined by Lender, and shall deposit with Lender at the Closing Date any positive escrow balance or amount reasonably required by Lender to establish the escrow (the "**Tax and Insurance Escrow**"). Lender shall have no obligation to ascertain whether any Imposition has been paid, and shall have no liability for any penalty or interest arising out of the payment obligations of Borrower.

**10.2 Capital Replacement Reserve.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender, on each Payment Date, the amount of Six Hundred Forty-Five and 83/100 Dollars ($645.83), being Twenty-Five Cents ($0.25) per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet of gross building area, divided by twelve (12) months (the "**Capital Replacement Reserve**"). **11.1 Environmental Covenants.** Borrower shall, at its sole cost and expense: (a) comply, and cause all tenants, occupants, contractors and agents at the Property to comply, with all Environmental Laws and with the LUR; (b) not cause or permit any release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under or from the Property that requires reporting, investigation, remediation or the imposition of any institutional control under any Environmental Law; (c) not permit any Person to conduct any activity at the Property that would reasonably be expected to result in the reopening of SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772 or the impairment of the No Further Action determination dated August 12, 2021; (d) maintain all institutional controls required by the LUR in full force and effect and in good working order; and (e) promptly deliver to Lender copies of all notices, orders, correspondence and reports received from or delivered to SCDHEC or any other environmental authority relating to the Property.

**11.4 Environmental Indemnity; Recourse.** Borrower and Guarantor have executed and delivered the Environmental Indemnity Agreement, which indemnifies Lender against all losses, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from or relating to the presence, release or threatened release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under or from the Property, and from any violation of the LUR or any Environmental Law. **11.5 Lender's Right to Cure Environmental Matters.** If Borrower fails to comply with this Article 11, or if Lender reasonably determines that immediate action is necessary to protect human health, the environment or the Collateral, Lender may, after such notice to Borrower as is reasonable under the circumstances (or without notice in an emergency), take such action as Lender deems necessary, including retaining environmental consultants, conducting investigations, implementing or maintaining institutional controls, communicating with SCDHEC, and performing remediation, and all costs and expenses so incurred, together with interest at the Default Rate, shall be Secured Obligations.

**11.6 No Reliance; No Representation by Lender.** Lender's acceptance of the Phase I ESA and any other environmental report shall not constitute a representation, warranty or acknowledgment by Lender as to the environmental condition of the Property, and Borrower acknowledges that Borrower has conducted its own investigation of the environmental condition of the Property and is not relying on Lender with respect thereto.

**11.7 Survival.** The obligations of Borrower under this Article 11 shall survive the repayment of the Loan, foreclosure, any conveyance in lieu of foreclosure and the release of this Mortgage, to the extent of any liability arising from conditions existing or acts occurring prior to such release.

**11.8 Event of Default.** Without limiting Section 14.1, the failure of Borrower to comply with Section 11.1 or Section 11.2, or the occurrence of any violation, modification or termination of the LUR, shall constitute an Event of Default (subject only to the cure period provided in Section 14.2(b), where applicable).
