# ARTICLE 8 — RENOVATION AND CONSTRUCTION

**8.1 The Renovation Holdback.** Lender shall hold the Renovation Holdback and shall disburse the same to Borrower from time to time in accordance with this Article 8 for the purpose of paying Renovation Costs (as defined in Section 8.2). Lender shall have no obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback unless and until each applicable condition in Section 8.5 has been satisfied. The Renovation Holdback is a portion of the Loan and bears interest from the Closing Date regardless of whether it has been disbursed, in accordance with the Note.

**8.2 Renovation Budget; Renovation Costs; Reallocations.** "**Renovation Costs**" means all hard and soft costs of completing the Renovation in accordance with the Plans, the GC Contract and the Renovation Budget, including the cost of construction, labor, materials, tenant improvement allowances, architects', engineers' and consultants' fees, permit and inspection fees, construction management fees, builder's risk and other insurance attributable to the Renovation, and the contingency set forth in the Renovation Budget. Borrower shall cause the Renovation to be completed in accordance with the Renovation Budget attached as **Exhibit D**. Borrower may reallocate amounts among line items of the Renovation Budget without Lender's consent, provided that (a) no reallocation increases the total Renovation Budget, (b) no reallocation increases the amount allocated to any line item by more than ten percent (10%) of such line item, (c) no reallocation decreases the contingent or soft-cost line items below the amounts shown on **Exhibit D**, and (d) Borrower delivers to Lender written notice of the reallocation within ten (10) business days. Any reallocation not satisfying the foregoing shall require Lender's prior written consent.

**8.3 Borrower Equity; Cost Overruns.** Borrower shall fund, from its own funds and not from Loan proceeds, the portion of the Renovation Costs not funded by the Renovation Holdback, being not less than Nine Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($900,000) (the "**Renovation Equity**"), together with all costs of the Renovation in excess of the Renovation Budget and all costs of completing the Renovation not funded by the Renovation Holdback. Borrower shall not be entitled to any reimbursement of the Renovation Equity from Loan proceeds. If at any time Lender reasonably determines that the undisbursed portion of the Renovation Holdback is insufficient to pay the remaining Renovation Costs, Borrower shall, within fifteen (15) days after Lender's written demand, deposit with Lender an amount equal to the deficiency, which amount shall be disbursed by Lender in accordance with this Article 8. Borrower shall fund its share of Renovation Costs such that at no time shall the aggregate amount disbursed from the Renovation Holdback exceed seventy-one and four hundred thirty-eight thousandths percent (71.438%) of the aggregate Renovation Costs incurred and certified to Lender as of such date (being the ratio of the Renovation Holdback, $2,250,000, to the Renovation Budget, $3,150,000).

**8.4 Draw Request Procedure.**

(a) Borrower may request a disbursement from the Renovation Holdback no more frequently than once per calendar month, by delivering to Lender a written draw request not less than ten (10) Business Days prior to the requested disbursement date.

(b) Each draw request shall be substantially in the form attached as **Exhibit E**, shall be signed by Borrower and certified by Borrower's architect of record, and shall include: (i) an AIA G702/G703 Application and Certificate for Payment detailing the work completed, the amounts previously paid, the amount currently requested and the percentage of completion; (ii) a schedule of the line items of the Renovation Budget to which the requested disbursement is to be applied and the remaining balance of each such line item; (iii) conditional lien waivers for the current draw and unconditional lien waivers for all prior draws from the General Contractor and each subcontractor performing work in an amount exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($25,000.00); (iv) a title date-down endorsement from the title insurer confirming that no intervening mechanics', materialmen's or other liens or encumbrances have been recorded against the Property since the date of this Mortgage or the most recent date-down endorsement, as applicable; (v) evidence of Lender's satisfactory inspection of the work in progress in accordance with Section 8.9; (vi) invoices or other evidence of the costs for which reimbursement is requested, to the extent reasonably requested by Lender; (vii) a certification that Borrower has funded its portion of Renovation Costs in accordance with Section 8.3; and (viii) such other information as Lender may reasonably request.

(c) Lender shall, within ten (10) Business Days after receipt of a complete and conforming draw request and satisfaction of the conditions in Section 8.5, disburse the requested amount, less the retainage required by Section 8.6, directly to Borrower or, at Lender's election, to the General Contractor, subcontractors, materialmen or other Persons entitled to payment, by joint check or otherwise.

**8.5 Conditions to Each Disbursement.** Lender's obligation to disburse any portion of the Renovation Holdback is subject to satisfaction of each of the following conditions, each in form and substance satisfactory to Lender:

(a) no Event of Default or event that with notice or lapse of time, or both, would constitute an Event of Default shall have occurred and be continuing;

(b) all representations and warranties in Article 5 shall be true and correct in all material respects;

(c) the Renovation shall be proceeding in accordance with the Plans and the Renovation Budget, and there shall exist no material defect, deficiency or departure from the Plans;

(d) each condition set forth in Section 8.4 shall have been satisfied and all documents required thereunder shall have been delivered to Lender;

(e) Borrower shall have funded the Renovation Equity in accordance with Section 8.3;

(f) no mechanics' or materialmen's lien shall have been filed against the Property and remain undischarged or unbonded, and the title insurer shall have issued the date-down endorsement required by Section 8.4(b)(iv);

(g) all building permits, Board of Architectural Review approvals (to the extent required for the work in question) and other governmental approvals required for the work shall have been obtained;

(h) if the work in question involves any penetration of, alteration to, or work within ten (10) feet of the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, Borrower shall have delivered to Lender (i) evidence of written notice to SCDHEC as required by the LUR, (ii) a vapor barrier protection and restoration plan prepared by a licensed environmental professional reasonably acceptable to Lender, and (iii) a certification from such professional that the vapor barrier has been inspected and, following the work, restored in accordance with the LUR; and

(i) Lender shall have received evidence that the undisbursed Renovation Holdback, together with Borrower's remaining unfunded Renovation Equity commitment, is sufficient to complete the Renovation in accordance with the Renovation Budget.

**8.6 Retainage.** Lender shall retain ten percent (10%) of each disbursement from the Renovation Holdback (the "**Retainage**") until Substantial Completion has been achieved in accordance with Section 8.11. Retainage shall be released in accordance with Section 8.15.

**8.7 Plans and Specifications; Permits; Board of Architectural Review.** The Renovation shall be performed in accordance with the Plans approved by Lender. Borrower shall not amend, modify or supplement the Plans in any manner that constitutes a Major Change (as defined in Section 8.8) without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall obtain and maintain in full force and effect all permits, licenses and approvals necessary for the Renovation, including any approval of the City of Charleston Board of Architectural Review applicable to the façade restoration and to the decorative iron balcony described in Section 5.14, and shall deliver copies thereof to Lender upon request.

**8.8 GC Contract; Change Orders.** Borrower has delivered to Lender a complete copy of the GC Contract, including all schedules, exhibits and amendments. Borrower shall not amend, modify, supplement, terminate or accept the assignment of the GC Contract, and shall not approve or enter into any change order, amendment or supplemental agreement under the GC Contract, without Lender's prior written consent if such action (a) increases the contract sum of the GC Contract or the Renovation Budget, (b) reduces the scope of the Renovation, (c) affects the structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, elevator or façade systems, (d) affects the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7 or the vapor barrier beneath such slab, or (e) would reasonably be expected to delay Substantial Completion beyond the Substantial Completion Deadline (each, a "**Major Change**"). Borrower hereby assigns to Lender, as part of the Collateral, all of Borrower's right, title and interest in, to and under the GC Contract and the Plans, and shall cause the General Contractor and Borrower's architect to execute and deliver to Lender a consent to such assignment and collateral assignment in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender.

**8.9 Inspections.** Lender, and any third-party inspector retained by Lender (at Borrower's expense), may inspect the Property and the work in progress at any reasonable time upon reasonable prior notice, and Borrower shall provide access and such information as Lender or its inspector may request. Borrower shall cause the work to be corrected promptly if any inspection discloses defective work or a departure from the Plans. Borrower acknowledges that no inspection by Lender shall constitute a waiver of any default, an approval of any work, or an assumption of responsibility for the adequacy, legality or quality of the Renovation, and that Lender has no duty to inspect.

**8.10 Mechanic's Liens; Lien Waivers; Title Date-Downs.** Borrower shall pay when due all costs of the Renovation and shall keep the Property free from mechanics', materialmen's and other liens. If any such lien is filed, Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days after notice thereof, cause the lien to be discharged of record or bonded over in a manner reasonably satisfactory to Lender and the title insurer. Borrower shall obtain unconditional lien waivers from the General Contractor and all subcontractors as a condition to each disbursement, and shall obtain a final title date-down endorsement and final lien waivers as a condition to the release of Retainage. Borrower shall not permit any stop notice, notice of nonpayment or similar claim to remain undischarged in a manner that could impair the Property or Lender's lien.

**8.11 Substantial Completion; Substantial Completion Deadline.** Borrower shall achieve Substantial Completion of the Renovation on or before June 15, 2026, time being of the essence. Borrower shall notify Lender in writing not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the anticipated date of Substantial Completion, and shall deliver to Lender (a) a certificate of Substantial Completion from Borrower's architect, (b) a copy of the certificate of occupancy (or equivalent) issued by the City of Charleston for the renovated portions of the Property, (c) a certification that the Renovation has been completed in accordance with the Plans and within the Renovation Budget, and (d) evidence that all costs of the Renovation have been paid or will be paid from the final disbursement. Failure to achieve Substantial Completion on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline shall constitute an Event of Default in accordance with Section 14.1(h) and shall entitle Lender to exercise its rights under the Completion Guaranty.

**8.12 Failure to Complete; Deemed Completion.** If Borrower fails to achieve Substantial Completion by the Substantial Completion Deadline, then, in addition to Lender's other remedies, Lender may (but shall not be obligated to) assume responsibility for completing the Renovation, and all amounts expended by Lender in doing so, together with interest at the Default Rate, shall be Secured Obligations. Lender's exercise of any right under this Section 8.12 shall not release Borrower or Guarantor from any obligation under the Loan Documents or the Completion Guaranty.

**8.13 Coordination with the LUR and Vapor Barrier.** Borrower shall cause the General Contractor, all subcontractors, Borrower's architect and all other Persons performing work at the Property to be informed in writing of the existence and location of the vapor barrier beneath the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, of the restrictions imposed by the LUR, and of the requirements of Section 11.3, prior to the commencement of any work at the Property. Borrower shall not permit any penetration, removal, alteration or compromise of the vapor barrier, and shall not permit any work affecting the Bay 1 slab, without (a) prior written notice to SCDHEC in accordance with the LUR, (b) Lender's prior written consent, and (c) supervision and post-work inspection and certification by a licensed environmental professional reasonably acceptable to Lender, all at Borrower's expense.

**8.14 No Obligation to Complete; No Lender Liability.** Lender shall have no obligation to complete the Renovation, to advance any amount in excess of the Renovation Holdback, or to pay any cost of the Renovation in excess of the amounts available in the Renovation Holdback and Borrower's Renovation Equity. Lender's approval of the Plans, the Renovation Budget, the GC Contract or any draw request, and any inspection by Lender or its consultant, shall not constitute a representation or warranty by Lender as to the adequacy, sufficiency, quality, legality or feasibility of the Renovation or the Plans, and Lender shall have no liability to Borrower or any other Person with respect thereto. Borrower acknowledges that Borrower, and not Lender, is the owner of the Property and the party responsible for the Renovation.

**8.15 Retainage Release; Final Disbursement.** Upon Lender's receipt of satisfactory evidence of Substantial Completion, final unconditional lien waivers from the General Contractor and all subcontractors and materialmen, a final title date-down endorsement, the certificate of occupancy, and confirmation that the vapor barrier and all LUR requirements have been satisfied, Lender shall release the Retainage and make the final disbursement from the Renovation Holdback. **8.16 Completion Guaranty.** The obligations of Borrower under this Article 8 are guaranteed by Guarantor pursuant to the Completion Guaranty, which guarantees completion of the Renovation within the Renovation Budget and on or before the Substantial Completion Deadline. Borrower's failure to achieve Substantial Completion by the Substantial Completion Deadline shall constitute a failure under the Completion Guaranty and an Event of Default under this Mortgage.

**8.17 No Waiver.** Acceptance by Borrower of any disbursement, or Lender's approval of any draw request, inspection report or plan, shall not constitute a waiver of any condition, covenant or Event of Default, or an approval of any work not conforming to the Plans.

Lender shall have no obligation to ascertain whether any Imposition has been paid, and shall have no liability for any penalty or interest arising out of the payment obligations of Borrower.

**10.2 Capital Replacement Reserve.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender, on each Payment Date, the amount of Six Hundred Forty-Five and 83/100 Dollars ($645.83), being Twenty-Five Cents ($0.25) per square foot per year multiplied by 31,000 square feet of gross building area, divided by twelve (12) months (the "**Capital Replacement Reserve**"). Funds in the Capital Replacement Reserve shall be disbursed to Borrower upon Lender's approval of qualifying capital expenditures, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed and shall be subject to Lender's reasonable review and approval procedures, including receipt of invoices, paid receipts and lien waivers for the completed work.

**10.3 Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve.** Borrower shall deposit with Lender at the Closing Date the sum of One Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($150,000.00) into a tenant improvement and leasing commission reserve account (the "**TI/LC Reserve**"). Disbursements from the TI/LC Reserve shall be subject to Lender's prior written approval, shall be made upon Lender's receipt of documentation reasonably acceptable to Lender, and shall be used exclusively for tenant improvement costs and leasing commissions incurred in connection with the leasing of vacant space at the Property. Upon any draw-down from the TI/LC Reserve, Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days after Lender's written demand, replenish the TI/LC Reserve to the full amount of One Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($150,000.00) from Borrower's own funds.

**10.4 Renovation Holdback.** The Renovation Holdback shall be held and disbursed in accordance with Article 8 and is not subject to this Article 10, except that Lender shall account for the Renovation Holdback in the same manner as the other reserves and escrows for record-keeping purposes.

**10.5 General Reserve Provisions.** All reserves and escrows shall be held by Lender in accounts maintained by Lender or by a depository institution acceptable to Lender, and may be commingled with other funds of Lender (including funds held for other borrowers). No interest shall be payable to Borrower on any reserve or escrow except as required by applicable law, and any interest actually earned shall be credited to the applicable account and applied as provided in this Article 10. All reserves and escrows shall be Collateral for the Secured Obligations and, at Lender's election upon an Event of Default, may be applied to the Secured Obligations in such order as Lender determines. Lender shall have no fiduciary obligation to Borrower with respect to any reserve or escrow, and any relationship created hereby is that of debtor and creditor. Lender may require additional reserves as a condition to any consent, waiver or amendment requested by Borrower.

**10.6 Failure to Deposit.** If Borrower fails to make any deposit required by this Article 10, Lender may, but shall not be obligated to, fund such deposit and the amount so funded shall be a Secured Obligation bearing interest at the Default Rate; provided that a failure to make any deposit required by this Article 10 that continues for five (5) Business Days after written notice from Lender shall constitute an Event of Default.

**10.7 Return of Reserves.** Upon the payment and performance in full of all Secured Obligations and the termination of Lender's commitment to make advances, Lender shall return to Borrower any balance remaining in the reserves and escrows, less any amounts applied or required to be applied to the Secured Obligations.

**10.8 Application to Secured Obligations.** At Lender's election upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Lender may apply any or all amounts held in the reserves and escrows to the Secured Obligations, whether or not then due.

# ARTICLE 11 — ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS AND THE LAND USE RESTRICTION

**11.1 Environmental Covenants.** Borrower shall, at its sole cost and expense: (a) comply, and cause all tenants, occupants, contractors and agents at the Property to comply, with all Environmental Laws and with the LUR; (b) not cause or permit any release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under or from the Property that requires reporting, investigation, remediation or the imposition of any institutional control under any Environmental Law; (c) not permit any Person to conduct any activity at the Property that would reasonably be expected to result in the reopening of SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772 or the impairment of the No Further Action determination dated August 12, 2021; (d) maintain all institutional controls required by the LUR in full force and effect and in good working order; and (e) promptly deliver to Lender copies of all notices, orders, correspondence and reports received from or delivered to SCDHEC or any other environmental authority relating to the Property.

**11.3 Notice Prior to Work Affecting Bay 1.** Borrower shall notify Lender and SCDHEC in writing not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the commencement of any work that will penetrate, disturb or come within ten (10) feet of the ground-floor slab of Bay 1 on Lot 7, and shall furnish Lender with the vapor barrier protection plan, the identity and qualifications of the environmental professional engaged to supervise the work, and the post-work certification described in Section 8.5(h).

**11.6 No Reliance; No Representation by Lender.** Lender's acceptance of the Phase I ESA and any other environmental report shall not constitute a representation, warranty or acknowledgment by Lender as to the environmental condition of the Property, and Borrower acknowledges that Borrower has conducted its own investigation of the environmental condition of the Property and is not relying on Lender with respect thereto.

**11.7 Survival.** The obligations of Borrower under this Article 11 shall survive the repayment of the Loan, foreclosure, any conveyance in lieu of foreclosure and the release of this Mortgage, to the extent of any liability arising from conditions existing or acts occurring prior to such release.

**11.8 Event of Default.** Without limiting Section 14.1, the failure of Borrower to comply with Section 11.1 or Section 11.2, or the occurrence of any violation, modification or termination of the LUR, shall constitute an Event of Default (subject only to the cure period provided in Section 14.2(b), where applicable).

    ("NOTARY","NOTARY ACKNOWLEDGMENT"),
    ("# EXHIBIT A","EXHIBIT A — LEGAL DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPERTY"),
    ("# EXHIBIT B","EXHIBIT B — RENT ROLL AND LEASE SUMMARY AS OF THE CLOSING DATE"),
    ("# EXHIBIT C","EXHIBIT C — PERMITTED EXCEPTIONS"),
    ("# EXHIBIT D","EXHIBIT D — RENOVATION BUDGET SUMMARY"),
    ("# EXHIBIT E","EXHIBIT E — FORM OF DRAW REQUEST AND ARCHITECT'S CERTIFICATE"),
    ("# EXHIBIT F","EXHIBIT F — FORM OF ANNUAL LAND USE RESTRICTION COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATE"),
]

def build_md(toc_pages):
    out = []
    for p in PARTS:
        out.append(Path(p).read_text())
    md = "\n".join(out)
    if toc_pages is None:
        lines = "\n".join(["x" for _ in TOC_ITEMS])
    else:
        lines = "\n".join(f"{label}\x09{pg}" for key,label in TOC_ITEMS for pg in [toc_pages.get(key,"")])
    md = md.replace("TOC_PLACEHOLDER", lines)
    Path("combined.md").write_text(md)
    return md

def set_font(run, name="Times New Roman", size=None, bold=None, italic=None, caps=False):
    run.font.name = name
    rpr = run._element.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = rpr.find(qn('w:rFonts'))
    if rf is None:
        rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts'); rpr.append(rf)
    for a in ('w:ascii','w:hAnsi','w:cs','w:eastAsia'):
        rf.set(qn(a), name)
    if size is not None: run.font.size = Pt(size)
    if bold is not None: run.font.bold = bold
    if italic is not None: run.font.italic = italic
    if caps: run.font.all_caps = True

def add_field(paragraph, instr):
    r = paragraph.add_run()
    fld = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld.set(qn('w:fldCharType'),'begin')
    r._element.append(fld)
    r2 = paragraph.add_run()
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'),'preserve'); it.text = instr
    r2._element.append(it)
    r3 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'),'separate')
    r3._element.append(fld2)
    r4 = paragraph.add_run("1")
    r5 = paragraph.add_run()
    fld3 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fld3.set(qn('w:fldCharType'),'end')
    r5._element.append(fld3)
    for rr in (r,r2,r3,r4,r5):
        set_font(rr, size=8.5)

def para(doc, text="", size=11, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, space_before=0, space_after=0, keep=False, caps=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(space_before); pf.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    pf.line_spacing = 1.0
    if keep: pf.keep_with_next = True
    if text:
        r = p.add_run(text); set_font(r, size=size, bold=bold, italic=italic, caps=caps)
    return p

def insert_before(doc, new_elements, ref_element):
    for el in new_elements:
        ref_element.addprevious(el)

def build(toc_pages, out_path):
    build_md(toc_pages)
    subprocess.run(["pandoc","-f","markdown-tex_math_dollars","-t","docx","combined.md","-o","body.docx"], check=True)
    doc = Document("body.docx")

    # page setup
    for s in doc.sections:
        s.page_width = Inches(8.5); s.page_height = Inches(11)
        s.left_margin = Inches(1.0); s.right_margin = Inches(1.0)
        s.top_margin = Inches(1.0); s.bottom_margin = Inches(1.0)
        s.different_first_page_header_footer = True

    # base styles
    st = doc.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = 'Times New Roman'; st.font.size = Pt(11)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    st.paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    rpr = st.element.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts')
    for a in ('w:ascii','w:hAnsi','w:cs','w:eastAsia'): rf.set(qn(a),'Times New Roman')
    rpr.append(rf)

    for name, size, before, after in (('Heading 1',12,20,10),('Title',20,0,12)):
        try:
            h = doc.styles[name]
        except KeyError:
            continue
        h.font.name='Times New Roman'; h.font.size=Pt(size); h.font.bold=True
        h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0,0,0)
        h.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(before); h.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(after)
        h.paragraph_format.keep_with_next=True
        h.paragraph_format.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
        h.paragraph_format.line_spacing=1.0

    # body tweaks: heading paragraphs, subparagraph indents, TOC
    body = doc.element.body
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        style = p.style.name if p.style is not None else ""
        if style == 'Heading 1':
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
            for r in p.runs: set_font(r, size=12, bold=True)
            # all caps headings
            txt = p.text.strip().upper()
            if p.text.strip() != txt and p.runs:
                p.runs[0].text = txt
                for r in p.runs[1:]: r.text = ""
            # page break before Exhibits and Signature
        txt = p.text.strip()
        if txt.startswith("(") and len(txt) > 2 and txt[2:3] == ")" and style=="Body Text":
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.35)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.0)
        if style == "Body Text" and txt and not txt.startswith("(") :
            pass

    # tables: grid + small font
    for tbl in doc.tables:
        try:
            tbl.style = doc.styles['Table Grid']
        except Exception:
            pass
        for row in tbl.rows:
            for cell in row.cells:

                    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
                    for r in p.runs: set_font(r, size=9)
        # header row bold

    def cp(text="", size=11, bold=False, italic=False, after=0):

        pf.space_before = Pt(0); pf.space_after = Pt(after); pf.line_spacing = 1.0
        if text:
            r = p.add_run(text); set_font(r, size=size, bold=bold, italic=italic)
        tmp.append(p)

    cp("", after=0)
    cp("", after=0)
    cp("MORTGAGE AND SECURITY AGREEMENT", size=22, bold=True, after=6)
    cp("(With Absolute Assignment of Leases and Rents)", size=12, italic=True, after=30)
    cp("by and from", size=11, italic=True, after=10)
    cp("PALMETTO GATEWAY PARTNERS LLC", size=13, bold=True, after=2)
    cp("a South Carolina limited liability company", size=11, after=10)
    cp("as Borrower and Mortgagor", size=11, italic=True, after=16)
    cp("to", size=11, italic=True, after=16)
    cp("CALVERLEY HERITAGE BANK", size=13, bold=True, after=2)
    cp("a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank", size=11, after=10)
    cp("as Lender and Mortgagee", size=11, italic=True, after=30)
    cp("Dated as of April 15, 2025", size=12, bold=True, after=30)
    cp("Property: 520–534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403", size=10.5, after=2)
    cp("Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008 and 460-12-04-009,", size=10.5, after=2)
    cp("together with the vacated Anson Lane strip, Charleston County, South Carolina", size=10.5, after=14)
    cp("Principal Amount Secured: $14,750,000.00", size=12, bold=True, after=2)
    cp("(including future advances of the Renovation Holdback)", size=10.5, italic=True, after=26)
    cp("RECORDING INFORMATION", size=10.5, bold=True, after=2)
    cp("To be recorded in the Office of the Register of Mesne Conveyances for Charleston County, South Carolina.", size=10, after=10)
    cp("AFTER RECORDING, RETURN TO: Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP, Charleston, South Carolina, Attn: Catherine Ashworth, Partner", size=10, after=10)
    cp("PREPARED BY: Fielding, Ashworth & Cole LLP, counsel for Lender", size=10, after=26)
    cp("DRAFT — MARCH 27, 2025 — PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO REVIEW AND COMMENT", size=9.5, bold=True, after=0)

    # page break paragraph at end of cover
    pb = doc.add_paragraph()
    pb.add_run().add_break(WD_BREAK.PAGE)
    tmp.append(pb)

    first = body[0]
    for el in tmp:
        first.addprevious(el._p)

    # ---- header / footer
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    hdr = sec.header
    hp = hdr.paragraphs[0]
    hp.text = ""
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    hr = hp.add_run("Mortgage and Security Agreement — Calverley Heritage Bank / Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC — DRAFT 03/27/2025")

    if sec.first_page_footer is not None:
        for p in sec.first_page_footer.paragraphs: p.text = ""
    doc.save(out_path)
    print("saved", out_path)

**FIELDING, ASHWORTH & COLE LLP**

Attorneys at Law — Charleston | Savannah

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT — PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION AND FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING LEGAL ADVICE**

# MEMORANDUM

| | |
|---|---|
| **TO:** | Catherine "Kit" Ashworth, Partner, Real Estate Practice Group Chair |
| **FROM:** | Jordan Vickers, Associate |
| **DATE:** | March 27, 2025 |
| **RE:** | Drafting Issues — Mortgage and Security Agreement, Calverley Heritage Bank / Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, $14,750,000 Commercial Real Estate Loan (CHB CRE Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047), 520–534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403 |
| **CC:** | File |
| **ENCLOSURE:** | Mortgage and Security Agreement (initial draft, 65 pages including Exhibits A–F) |

# 1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND SUMMARY OF CONCLUSIONS

**1.1 Purpose.** This memorandum accompanies the initial draft of the Mortgage and Security Agreement (the "**Draft Mortgage**") for the captioned loan (the "**Loan**") and records (a) the issues identified in the source record before and during drafting, (b) the independent recomputation of every figure, date and ratio used in the Draft Mortgage, (c) the drafting decisions taken, including provisions added beyond the executed Term Sheet, and (d) the items that must be resolved or documented by the client before the Draft Mortgage is circulated to borrower's counsel or executed. It responds to your markup notes of March 18, 2025 and addresses each instruction item in turn.

**1.2 Scope and standard.** The record consists of the eight documents listed in Section 2. All statements of fact in this memorandum are cited to the source document and section. No fact has been assumed without labeling it; where the record is silent, the gap is identified rather than filled. All arithmetic has been recomputed from source components and not taken from any summary or prior calculation.

**1.3 Summary of conclusions.** The Draft Mortgage is in a form suitable for internal partner review. The instrument is not, however, ready to be sent to borrower's counsel in its present state, and the Loan should not close, until four matters are resolved:

> **(a) Loan sizing and credit approval.** The file's own projections do not support a $14,750,000 loan at the stated terms. Even on the most favorable stabilized assumptions in the rent roll, projected net operating income ($622,772) produces a debt service coverage ratio of 0.55x on the post-interest-only amortizing debt service and 0.72x on interest-only debt service, against a required 1.25x. The appraisal's income approach likewise does not reconcile to its concluded values (implied capitalisation rates of 1.86% as-is and 2.52% as-stabilized, against the 5.75%–6.50% range the appraiser identifies as market). The DSCR covenant in Article 12 will be breached at the first test date as a matter of arithmetic. A documented credit approval or exception is required before we finalize the covenant, the cure mechanism and the cash management provisions.
>
> **(b) Execution authority.** Borrower's Operating Agreement requires the approval of Members holding at least 75% of the membership interests for any financing in excess of $1,000,000. Graydon Development Group LLC holds 72%. Mr. Graydon's signature alone, through GDG as Managing Member, is therefore not sufficient authority to execute the Mortgage and the other Loan Documents. Certified written consents of GDG plus at least one Passive Member (and ideally all three Members) must be obtained, and the title company will require the same evidence under Requirement 8 of the commitment.
>
> **(c) Single-purpose entity and Operating Agreement Amendment.** The Operating Agreement contains none of the single-purpose entity provisions the Term Sheet requires (no independent manager, no bankruptcy consent, no separateness covenants, no single-purpose purpose clause, no change-of-control restriction). The Draft Mortgage assumes the amendment is delivered as a closing condition and is executed by all three Members. Tidewater GP Holdings LLC's authority to bind Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC's governing documents, are not in the record.
>
> **(d) Title to the Anson Lane strip and the SCDHEC land use restriction.** The strip is insured as part of the fee estate on the face of the commitment but was conveyed by quitclaim deed only, and the title officer expressly reserves the right to charge an additional premium or limit coverage by endorsement. Affirmative coverage must be negotiated and confirmed before closing (see Section 5.1). The land use restriction on Lot 7 requires bespoke covenants, an event of default and reporting mechanics, which the Draft Mortgage contains in Articles 8 and 11 (see Section 5.2).

**1.4 Format implications.** The Draft Mortgage incorporates an absolute assignment of leases and rents (Article 4) rather than a separate instrument, as you directed; it contains a self-contained yield maintenance formula (Article 13) built on the Term Sheet rather than on the formulation in your notes, which I recommend against adopting as drafted (see Section 7.1); and it does not grant a power of sale (Section 14.4).

# 2. SOURCE INVENTORY AND METHODOLOGY

**2.1 Inventory.** The following documents were reviewed in full. No other documents were provided.

| # | Document | Date | Prepared by | Principal use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Term Sheet — Commercial Real Estate Loan (executed, binding) | April 1, 2025 | Calverley Heritage Bank / Borrower | Controlling business terms; basis for every substantive provision |
| 2 | Commitment for Title Insurance No. PT-2025-04-1178 | Effective February 28, 2025 | Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC for Commonwealth National Title Underwriters Inc. | Legal description; Permitted Exceptions; requirements 1–12; closer's notes |
| 3 | Appraisal Summary Report (File PVS-2025-0214-CHS) | February 14, 2025 | Pinnacle Valuation Services LLC | Values, occupancy, rent roll, market data |
| 4 | Phase I ESA Executive Summary, Report CLR-2025-0119 | January 28, 2025 | Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC | CREC, SCDHEC NFA letter, land use restriction and vapor barrier |
| 5 | Redacted Summary of Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC | Effective January 12, 2024; amended through March 1, 2025 | Cartwright & Lyons LLP (borrower's counsel) | Authority, Major Decisions, SPE gaps, transfer restrictions |
| 6 | Rent Roll and Lease Abstracts (3 tabs: Summary; Lease Abstracts; Vacancy Schedule) | Undated (current as of closing preparations) | Borrower's managing member | Leases, escalations, ROFR, estoppel/SNDA obligations, NOI and DSCR projections |
| 7 | Renovation Budget and Draw Schedule (2 tabs: Budget Detail; Draw Schedule) | Undated | Borrower's managing member | Renovation Budget, holdback allocation, 14-month draw schedule |
| 8 | Internal memorandum — Markup Notes (Kit Ashworth to Jordan Vickers) | March 18, 2025 | This firm | Drafting instructions |

**2.2 Documents referenced in the record but not provided.** The executed GC Contract with Beaufort Builders Group LLC; the ALTA/NSPS survey by Cartwright Land Surveying LLC dated January 15, 2025 (referenced in the title commitment and the appraiser's assumptions); the unredacted Operating Agreement and the March 1, 2025 amendment; the full Phase I ESA report and appendices (only the executive summary is in the file); the SCDHEC file and No Further Action letter; the recorded land use restriction (Deed Book 1203, Page 89); the form of Guaranty, Completion Guaranty, Interest Shortfall Guaranty and Environmental Indemnity Agreement; Guarantor's personal financial statement; any City of Charleston encroachment license for the King Street balcony; the full appraisal report; and any loan committee approval or credit exception memorandum. Each is carried forward in Section 11.

**2.3 Methodology.** I extracted every figure, date and obligation from the record into an issue log with a source citation, recomputed the arithmetic independently (Section 9), drafted the instrument from the verified log, and then re-read the instrument against the log to confirm that (i) each Term Sheet requirement is implemented or expressly noted as not implemented, (ii) each defined term is used consistently, (iii) every internal cross-reference resolves (verified programmatically: 175 defined sections, no broken section or article references), and (iv) no figure in the instrument differs from the verified figure without a flagged explanation.

**2.4 Character of the record.** The record contains several internal contradictions that cannot be resolved on the documents: two occupancy figures, two rent figures per lease, two DSCR test dates, two flood map panel numbers, two registered agent names, three different interest-shortfall/amortisation assumptions in the draw schedule and the vacancy schedule, and an appraisal whose income approach is irreconcilable with its value conclusion. In each case I have adopted the figure that the controlling document (the Term Sheet) or the more granular record supports, disclosed the conflict in the instrument where appropriate, and flagged the item here for your decision. I have not silently chosen a figure or invented a fact.

# 3. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — TOP-RISK REGISTER

The following register is ordered by risk. Each item is developed in the section indicated. "Draft" indicates the treatment in the Draft Mortgage.

| 4 | SPE provisions absent from Operating Agreement (no independent manager, bankruptcy consent, separateness, single-purpose purpose) | Critical | Operating Agreement §§1.4, 3.1, 3.2, 8.1, 9.1; Term Sheet §10.1 | Bankruptcy remoteness defeated; SPE representations in Draft Mortgage untrue at closing | §6.2; Draft Mortgage §§6.12, 7.6 |

| 6 | SCDHEC land use restriction: no residential use of Lot 7 ground floor; vapor barrier maintenance and periodic inspection | High | Title Exception 4 and Closer's note 1; Phase I ESA §§5.3, 6(d) | Regulatory reopening, remediation cost, lender liability; renovation scope may breach the LUR | §5.2; Draft Mortgage Arts. 8.13, 11 |
| 7 | Tenant estoppels and SNDAs are closing conditions but the Lowcountry Provisions lease contains no estoppel, SNDA or assignment provision | High | Term Sheet §§2.3, 12.1(j)–(k); Rent Roll, Lease Abstracts (Bay 1) | Condition precedent cannot be compelled; rents assignment enforcement contested; SNDA coverage gap | §5.4; Draft Mortgage §§4.4, 6.7(c) |

# 4. CREDIT CAPACITY, VALUATION AND LOAN SIZING

The four issues in this section are analytical rather than drafting points in the narrow sense, but they determine whether the covenant, reserve and cure architecture we have drafted can function. I have recomputed each figure from source components.

**4.1 Debt service capacity and the DSCR covenant — recomputation.**

**Source components.** Loan $14,750,000 (Term Sheet §3.1); interest rate Daily SOFR plus 285 basis points with a 3.00% SOFR floor, i.e. 5.85% at the floor (Term Sheet §3.6); interest-only for months 1–24, then 25-year amortisation from May 15, 2027 (Term Sheet §3.9); DSCR covenant of 1.25x beginning after month 24 (Term Sheet §7.1); stabilized NOI of $622,772 on the borrower's best-case projection (Rent Roll, Vacancy Schedule rows 8–18, being $755,549 gross revenue less $37,777 vacancy/credit loss less $95,000 net landlord expense burden).

**Recomputation.**

| Metric | Amount | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Annual interest during interest-only period | $862,875 | $14,750,000 × 5.85% (the rent roll shows $863,375 — a $500 rounding error in the file) |
| Monthly payment, 25-year amortisation at 5.85% | $93,686.61 | Standard amortisation formula, 300 periods |
| Annual debt service after the interest-only period | $1,124,239 | $93,686.61 × 12 (the rent roll shows $1,122,000 — understated by $2,239) |
| DSCR on amortising debt service | **0.55x** | $622,772 ÷ $1,124,239 |
| DSCR on interest-only debt service | **0.72x** | $622,772 ÷ $862,875 |
| NOI required to meet 1.25x on amortising debt service | **$1,405,299** | $1,124,239 × 1.25 |
| NOI required to meet 1.25x on interest-only debt service | **$1,078,594** | $862,875 × 1.25 |
| Shortfall against the amortising requirement | $782,527 (125.6%) | $1,405,299 − $622,772 |
| Debt yield | **4.22%** | $622,772 ÷ $14,750,000 |
| Loan size supported at 1.25x DSCR (25-year amortisation, 5.85%) | ≈ **$6,536,000** | $622,772 ÷ 1.25 ÷ 0.0762196 |
| Loan size supported at a 9.0% debt yield | ≈ **$6,920,000** | $622,772 ÷ 0.09 |

**Conclusion.** On the file's own numbers the Loan is approximately twice the size that the Property's income supports. The interest due during the interest-only period ($862,875) exceeds the Property's projected gross revenue at stabilized occupancy ($755,549). The Vacancy Schedule states the same conclusion in terms (row 25: "DOES NOT MEET 1.25x COVENANT"; row 39: "DSCR compliance at month 24 is at significant risk regardless of lease-up pace"). The Term Sheet's own requirement for an Interest Shortfall Guaranty covering the first fourteen months after closing (Term Sheet §5.5(c)) is consistent with — and corroborates — the proposition that the parties expect the Property not to cover debt service during the renovation and lease-up period.

**Options, for your discussion with Marcus Prideaux.** (i) Reduce the loan amount to a supportable level; (ii) lengthen the interest-only period to or beyond the first DSCR test date and reset the covenant (the Term Sheet already ends interest-only at month 24, one month before amortisation begins in the same window in which the covenant is first tested); (iii) retain the loan amount but require a DSCR cure deposit, a cash-management sweep at a sub-1.10x trigger and an extension of the Interest Shortfall Guaranty through at least the first test date; (iv) treat the DSCR covenant as a placeholder and obtain a documented credit exception. What we should not do is paper the covenant as drafted and say nothing: a covenant that fails on the closing-date projections is either a default trigger from day one or evidence that the covenant was not intended to be enforced, and neither posture serves the Bank well in a workout. **Draft:** Article 12 implements the covenant precisely (Section 12.1), defines Net Operating Income and Annual Debt Service (Section 1.1), and adds a limited DSCR cure right (Section 12.6) — the Term Sheet's "without cure" language in §11.1(i) presupposes a cure mechanic that the Term Sheet never supplies. The cure mechanic is our construct and requires your approval (Section 10).

**4.2 The appraisal does not reconcile to its own income approach.**

| Appraisal input | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Concluded as-is value | $18,200,000 | Appraisal §1, §6.2, §7 |
| Concluded as-stabilized value | $23,500,000 | Appraisal §1, §6.3, §7 |
| Selected going-in capitalisation rate (as-is) | 6.25% | Appraisal §6.2 |
| Selected capitalisation rate (as-stabilized) | 5.85% | Appraisal §6.3 |
| Stated as-is NOI | $332,000–$345,000 | Appraisal §6.2 |
| Stated stabilized NOI | $582,000–$592,000 | Appraisal §6.3 |

**Recomputation.** A 6.25% capitalisation rate applied to NOI of $332,000–$345,000 indicates a value of **$5,312,000–$5,520,000**, not $18,200,000. A 5.85% rate applied to stabilized NOI of $582,000–$592,000 indicates a value of **$9,948,718–$10,119,658**, not $23,500,000. Put the other way, the concluded values imply NOI of **$1,137,500** (as-is) and **$1,374,750** (as-stabilized) — between 2.3 and 3.4 times the NOI the appraiser reports. The implied capitalisation rates on the reported NOI are **1.86%** (as-is) and **2.52%** (as-stabilized), both far outside the 5.75%–6.50% range the appraiser says is market (Appraisal §4).

**Consequence.** The as-is loan-to-value ratio of 81.04% (Term Sheet §3.5; Appraisal §7) — and the Bank's reliance on it — rests on a value conclusion that its own income approach does not support. Either the NOI figures or the value conclusions are wrong; the discrepancy is not a rounding matter. Term Sheet §12.1(d) makes receipt of a satisfactory appraisal "supporting the as-is and as-stabilized values set forth in Section 2.4" a condition precedent to closing, and the appraisal must conform to USPAP and FIRREA. **Recommendation:** return the report to Pinnacle Valuation Services for correction or a written reconciliation of the income approach to the concluded values, and obtain an independent review appraisal under the Bank's appraisal policy before closing. This is also the answer to the question you raised with Marcus about whether the as-is LTV "runs a little hot": at 81.04% it is well above customary CRE leverage, and 82.87% of the purchase price ($14,750,000 ÷ $17,800,000), and on the appraiser's own income figures the ratio would exceed 100%.

**4.3 Occupancy and in-place rent — three conflicting sets of figures.**

| Item | Term Sheet §2.3 | Appraisal §§1, 3.1 | Rent Roll (Summary tab) | Recomputation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Occupied area | 21,400 SF | 21,400 SF | 17,400 SF | 3,800 + 3,800 + 9,800 = **17,400 SF** |
| Occupancy rate | 68% | 68% | 56.13% | 17,400 ÷ 31,000 = **56.13%** (21,400 ÷ 31,000 = 69.03%, so 21,400 and 68% are also inconsistent with each other) |
| Vacant area | 13,600 SF (43.9%) | 32% | 13,600 SF (43.87%) | 13,600 ÷ 31,000 = **43.87%** — note 68% plus 43.9% equals 111.9% |
| Total in-place annual rent | $415,100 | $415,100 | $415,100 | Sum of the three leases at stated rents = **$415,100** |
| Weighted average rent | not stated | $19.40/SF | $23.86/SF | $415,100 ÷ 17,400 = **$23.86/SF** ($415,100 ÷ 21,400 = $19.40/SF, which confirms the appraisal used the erroneous 21,400 SF) |

The Term Sheet's §2.3 contradictory within itself: it states occupancy of "approximately sixty-eight percent (68%)" and, three sentences later, that vacant space totals 13,600 square feet "or approximately 43.9% of total building area." Both statements cannot be true. The correct figures are 17,400 SF occupied, 56.13%.

**Separate but related: the rents.** The Rent Roll's Summary and Lease Abstracts tabs state the "current" base rents as $28.50/SF (Bay 1), $24.00/SF (Bay 3) and $22.00/SF (Suite A), totalling $415,100. The same tabs' escalation schedules show Bay 1 escalating 3% annually "beginning January 1, 2025" (i.e. $29.355/SF, $111,549 per annum) and Bay 3 escalating 2.5% annually "beginning July 1, 2023" (i.e. $25.215/SF, $95,817–$95,836 per annum depending on rounding). The Vacancy Schedule in fact uses $111,549 for Bay 1. The rent actually payable as of an April 15, 2025 closing, applying the contractual escalations, is therefore approximately **$422,985**, not $415,100 — a difference of $7,885 per annum that flows directly into the DSCR calculation. **Draft:** Exhibit B to the Draft Mortgage reports the lease-stated rents of $415,100 (as the record's certified rent roll) and Note 10 to Exhibit B discloses the escalation conflict, states the escalated total of $422,985, and requires Borrower to certify the conformed rent roll on or before closing. The Section 5.4 representation must not be made against a rent roll that the borrower's own document contradicts.

**4.4 Sources and uses — the closing costs are unfunded.**

| Use of funds | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase price | $17,800,000 | Term Sheet §§3.2, 3.4 |
| Renovation Budget | $3,150,000 | Term Sheet §3.4; Renovation Budget |
| **Total Project Cost (as defined)** | **$20,950,000** | Term Sheet §3.4 |

| Source of funds | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Loan (Initial Advance $12,500,000 + Renovation Holdback $2,250,000) | $14,750,000 | Term Sheet §3.3 |
| Borrower Equity Contribution | $6,200,000 | Term Sheet §3.4 |
| **Total** | **$20,950,000** | |

The sources equal the uses exactly — which is the problem. The Total Project Cost as defined excludes (i) closing costs that Term Sheet §13.2 requires Borrower to pay, including the origination fee of $147,500 (Term Sheet §13.1), South Carolina mortgage recording tax of $54,575 (0.37% of $14,750,000, as you computed), title premiums, survey, appraisal, environmental and legal fees, and UCC filing and search fees; (ii) the $150,000 TI/LC Reserve required to be deposited at closing (Term Sheet §6.3); and (iii) any initial deposit into the tax and insurance escrow (Term Sheet §6.1). At closing, the Initial Advance of $12,500,000 plus the $6,200,000 equity contribution produces $18,700,000 against a purchase price of $17,800,000, leaving exactly $900,000 — which is precisely the Renovation Equity that the Draw Schedule deploys over fourteen months (Renovation Budget, Budget Detail row 9; Draw Schedule column S). On these numbers there is no source for closing costs and no source for the TI/LC Reserve. The gap is approximately **$450,000–$600,000** depending on title premium and escrow deposits (my estimate, to be confirmed from the closing/settlement statement). **Recommendation:** require an updated sources-and-uses statement and evidence of additional Borrower equity before closing; add the TI/LC Reserve funding to the closing conditions; and confirm with Prestige Title the recording fee and mortgage tax computation (Term Sheet §13.2(f)).

# 5. TITLE, SURVEY AND COLLATERAL ISSUES

**5.1 The Anson Lane strip — quitclaim vesting (your item 2).** You asked three questions. Answering them on the face of the commitment:

> **(1) Is the strip insured without a carve-out?** Yes, on the face of the commitment. Schedule A, Section 4 describes Parcel Two as part of the land and Section 3 confirms fee simple vesting in Hampstead Village Holdings LLC as to both parcels; Schedule B, Part II contains no exception that excepts the strip, reduces the estate to less than fee simple, or qualifies the strip's coverage. The general exceptions (a)–(e) are the printed standard exceptions, which are committed to be removed upon delivery of the survey, affidavits, gap indemnity and lien waivers (Schedule B, Part II, Exception 1; Requirements 9, 10 and 12).
>
> **(2) Is the vesting chain complete?** On the title company's examination, yes: Quitclaim Deed from the City of Charleston dated February 28, 2019, recorded March 22, 2019, in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, pursuant to Ordinance No. 2019-084. But the title officer expressly qualifies this: "This parcel was conveyed by Quitclaim Deed only … no warranties of title were provided … The Company's willingness to insure title to this parcel … should not be construed as a representation that the chain of title for this parcel is equivalent to that of Parcel One" (Vesting Chain Notes, item 2).
>
> **(3) Should we request an endorsement?** Yes, but note two points. First, the endorsement the title officer recommends is an ALTA 34 (Identified Exception) or other affirmative coverage specific to the parcel (Closer's Note 3), not the ALTA 9 you mentioned in your notes; ALTA 9 covers restrictions, encroachments and mineral rights and does not address quitclaim vesting. Second, the title officer reserves the right to require an additional premium for extended coverage and/or to limit coverage by endorsement on this parcel (Closer's Note 3). We should obtain written confirmation, before closing, of the precise form of affirmative coverage, the premium, and that no endorsement will limit the amount of insurance as to the strip.

**Why it matters.** The strip runs along the rear (northwest) boundary of Lots 7, 8 and 9 and provides rear access and loading for the building (Phase I ESA §2, "Physical Description of Lots"; Appraisal §2.1). Loss of, or a dispute over, the strip would impair vehicular and pedestrian access and the approved site plan — the concern you flagged. **Draft:** Section 5.3 of the Draft Mortgage contains a specific representation addressed to the quitclaim conveyance and to Borrower's title to the strip; Section 3.1(a) describes Parcel Two in the granting clause with both the ordinance and the deed references; Exhibit A carries both parcels and the Cartwright plat reference. **5.2 The SCDHEC land use restriction and the controlled recognized environmental condition.**

The appraiser treats it as minor but notes that any City-mandated removal could affect the historic façade and require work beyond the current budget (Appraisal §§2.1, 2.2). The façade restoration line item of $625,000 expressly includes "decorative ironwork repair (including King Street balcony)" (Renovation Budget, Budget Detail line 3) and is subject to Board of Architectural Review oversight.

**Issues.** (i) The encroachment remains a title exception unless affirmative coverage is obtained; (ii) there is no encroachment license in the record, so the City's position is unknown; (iii) the renovation scope touches the balcony, which may require the City to confirm or condition the license, and removal (if required) is an unbudgeted cost; (iv) a municipal removal order would not be a taking and would not produce condemnation proceeds. **Draft:** Section 5.14 (representation disclosing the encroachment), Section 6.5 (compliance with permits and obligation to maintain the encroachment license), Section 8.7 (BAR approvals), and the Permitted Exceptions schedule (Exhibit C, item 4). **Action:** request evidence of the encroachment license now and make delivery of the license (or a written statement from the City that no license is required for the existing balcony) a closing condition. Consider also making the ALTA 28.1 endorsement a closing condition, since the Term Sheet §5.6 already requires "such endorsements as Lender may reasonably require."

**5.4 Leases, estoppels, SNDAs and the Bay 2 right of first refusal.**

**Facts.** Three leases are in place (Exhibit B to the Draft Mortgage; Rent Roll, Lease Abstracts):

> • **Lowcountry Provisions Inc.** (Bay 1; 3,800 SF; NNN; expires December 31, 2027). The lease contains **no assignment or subletting provision**, **no estoppel certificate obligation** and **no subordination or SNDA provision**. The tenant holds an exclusive right to use as a specialty grocery within the Property. The abstract notes "Assignment/Subletting: No provision."
>
> • **Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC** (Bay 3; 3,800 SF; modified gross; expires June 30, 2026). Assignment requires consent not unreasonably withheld; estoppel within 15 business days of request; lease is subordinate to any mortgage **provided the mortgagee delivers a commercially reasonable non-disturbance agreement**. The tenant holds a **right of first refusal on Bay 2** (15 business day acceptance period) which survives renewal. A three-year renewal option requires notice by December 31, 2025. The lease's early termination right (effective June 30, 2025) required notice by December 31, 2024, which has passed, so the right has lapsed.
>
> • **Tidemark Consulting Group LLC** (Suite A; 9,800 SF; NNN; expires March 31, 2029). Assignment requires consent which may be withheld in the landlord's sole discretion; estoppel within 10 business days; tenant agrees to execute an SNDA upon request.

**Issues.**

> **(a) Closing conditions depend on third parties.** Term Sheet §§2.3 and 12.1(j)–(k) require estoppel certificates and SNDAs from all three tenants as conditions precedent. Two of the three leases obligate the tenant to deliver an estoppel on request (and Harmon & Wren's lease conditions its subordination on receipt of a commercially reasonable non-disturbance agreement), but the Lowcountry lease obligates the tenant to do neither. The condition can therefore only be satisfied with that tenant's voluntary cooperation. You are right that the Lowcountry estoppel should not be waived; the Draft Mortgage accordingly makes delivery of the estoppels a condition to the Initial Advance (Section 6.7(c)) and, because the tenant cannot be compelled, couples it with a commercially reasonable efforts covenant rather than an absolute obligation that Borrower would breach at closing. **Action:** Marcus should be told that the Lowcountry estoppel and SNDA are outside Borrower's control and that the Bank's options are to waive or to delay closing.
>
> **(b) The Bank must decide whether it will give non-disturbance.** Because the pre-existing leases are prior in time to the Mortgage, foreclosure will not extinguish them unless they are subordinated. Harmon & Wren's and Tidemark's leases subordinate only in exchange for a commercially reasonable non-disturbance agreement. The Lowcountry lease is silent, so its position on foreclosure is unresolved. The Draft Mortgage therefore (i) subordinates the leases to the Mortgage (§4.5), (ii) requires Borrower to use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver SNDAs (§4.4), and (iii) preserves Lender's discretion whether to deliver a non-disturbance agreement (§4.5).
>
> **(c) The Bay 2 right of first refusal affects the collateral and any foreclosure purchaser.** The ROFR constrains lease-up of Bay 2 (the appraiser adds 60–90 days to the absorption timeline, Appraisal §§3.2, 6.3; the Vacancy Schedule notes the marketing constraint) and, if not subordinated, would bind a purchaser at foreclosure. Section 4.5 of the Draft Mortgage provides that any SNDA delivered by Lender may provide that purchase rights of this kind are not binding on Lender or a foreclosure purchaser. **Action:** obtain that provision in the Harmon & Wren SNDA; also confirm that the $550,000 TI allowance line covers the Bay 2 build-out notwithstanding the ROFR process.
>
> **(d) The assignment of rents and the Lowcountry lease.** You are correct that, under the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act, the assignment is enforceable against a tenant upon notification irrespective of the lease's silence on assignment. The Draft Mortgage implements this as an absolute and present assignment (Article 4), with the statutory basis identified, a revocable licence to collect until default (§4.2), enforcement on default without court order or receiver (§4.3), tenant direction letters and estoppels (§4.4), and an express representation that Borrower has full right and authority to assign all rents, naming the Lowcountry lease (§5.4). **Verification required:** the citation you used (§ 29-3-100 et seq.) should be verified against the current Code before the instrument is recorded; the Draft Mortgage refers to the Act by name and to Title 29, Chapter 3 rather than to a specific section range, and we should confirm the statutory requirements (effectiveness on execution and recording, perfection by recording, enforcement upon default) in the research file.

**5.5 Survey, legal description and Permitted Exceptions.**

> **(a) No metes and bounds in the record.** The Term Sheet's Exhibit A is a summary description by plat reference; the commitment's Schedule A describes Parcel One by plat reference and Parcel Two by ordinance, deed and the Cartwright plat (Plat Book 64, Page 91). The ALTA/NSPS survey itself is not in the file and is a closing requirement (Requirement 9; Term Sheet §12.1(e)). Exhibit A to the Draft Mortgage therefore carries the commitment description and the plat references, with a clearly bracketed instruction for the metes and bounds to be inserted from the certified survey. **This is the only substantive blank in the instrument** (Section 12). Do not record until it is conformed.
>
> **(b) Survey recertification timing.** Requirement 9 requires a survey "dated or re-certified to a date not more than ninety (90) days prior to the date of closing." The survey is dated January 15, 2025. Ninety days later is April 15, 2025 — the anticipated closing date exactly. Any slippage in closing requires recertification, and the Term Sheet permits closing as late as May 15, 2025 (Term Sheet §14.5). Request recertification now.
>
> **(c) Permitted Exceptions require Lender's written approval.** Neither the Term Sheet nor the commitment defines which Schedule B, Part II exceptions the Bank accepts. The Draft Mortgage defines "Permitted Exceptions" by reference to Lender's written approval and attaches **Exhibit C**, which lists the six specific exceptions and reserves item 7 for such further matters as Lender may approve. **Action:** obtain Marcus's written approval of Exhibit C before closing, and confirm that the standard exceptions (a)–(e) are deleted by endorsement as the commitment contemplates.
>
> **(d) Future advances and mechanics' lien priority.** The Renovation Holdback is a future advance under a recorded mortgage. Section 3.4 of the Draft Mortgage contains the future-advance clause and a maximum principal amount of $14,750,000; the Term Sheet requires a future advance endorsement (Term Sheet §5.6). During construction, the Bank's priority over subsequently recorded mechanics' liens depends on the future-advance endorsement and on the draw mechanics (date-down endorsements, lien waivers, retainage) — see Section 8.5 below.
>
> **(e) Tax parcels and the escrow.** Three tax map numbers are identified, but the vacated Anson Lane strip has no separate tax map number in the record; it may be assessed within Lot 7 or separately. Term Sheet §6.1 requires the escrow to cover "all three tax parcels." **Action:** confirm from the tax certificates (Requirement 10) how the strip is assessed, and conform the escrow provision and Exhibit A accordingly.
